title: Nepal flood rescue efforts intensify as number of missing soars past 2,000
summary: Rescuers pulled out survivors and helicopters ferried people to safety as Nepal and China raced to respond after catastrophic flash floods​ killed hundreds of people.
story: Rescuers pulled out survivors caked in dark brown mud and helicopters lifted stranded people to safety Friday as Nepal and China raced to respond after catastrophic flash floods and landslides killed almost 600 people and left roughly 2,500 missing.

Nepali and Chinese authorities warned of further risk of flooding from a new lake that has formed upstream following Wednesday's disaster, telling people in the potentially affected areas to move to safer ground.

More than 3,700 people have been rescued in Nepal so far, but 1,924 people remain unaccounted for in the country, according to authorities. China's state media previously said 558 people were missing on the Chinese side.

Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said Friday that the confirmed death toll had risen to 579. Local Nepalese media said there could still be as many as 12,000 people unaccounted for, but that much higher figure was not confirmed by any officials. Hundreds of the missing are foreigners who were in the area to work, trek or make a pilgrimage to a sacred peak on the Tibet side of the border.

Helicopters had carried more than 3,000 people to safety in Kathmandu and other locations. On the Chinese side, there was little information about survivors, although the death toll rose to five Friday as state media showed evacuations of villages and leaders' efforts to direct relief efforts.

The Red Cross said Friday that some 90,000 people had likely been impacted by the flooding, which is believed to have been triggered by the collapse of a rocky ledge and the vast portion of a glacier it had supported.

The Nepal Police issued a fresh alert Friday after receiving information that a dam on the Tibetan side of the border was running over. Security personnel and rescue and relief workers were told to stay on high alert and immediately move to a safe location if necessary.

It was unclear if that concern was related to fears of flooding from an overflowing barrier lake that formed behind a dam formed by debris from the initial flash floods, high up on the Chinese side of the Himalayan mountains.
Nepal police spokesperson Abi Narayan Kafle said the rescue operation "hasn't stopped," but was continuing under high alert.

Although Chinese state broadcaster CCTV reported Friday that the lake was more than 6 miles from Gyirong Port, the border crossing with Nepal that was decimated by a wall of mud and water on Wednesday morning, it said the risk of flooding was high. It said the lake was at an elevation of 9,680 feet, about 3,280 feet above Gyirong Port.
CCTV later said flood risks from the overflowing lake were deemed "manageable," Reuters reported.
Nepali army rescuers were working to help people trapped in a hydropower tunnel in Rasuwa, part of the Upper Trishuli-1 Hydropower Project.
In video from the scene, rescuers half-pulled, half-pushed a man covered in dark brown mud out of the tunnel. He was one of dozens who were likely trapped inside.
Army spokesperson Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet told The Associated Press the focus was on survivors.
"It is complicated to find the entry and exit points of the tunnel because everything has been covered by mud," Basnet said. "Our first priority is rescuing the stranded people."
What caused the flash floods?

Scientists said satellite images indicated that bedrock underneath a glacier high in the Himalayan region had collapsed, taking part of the glacier with it. The rockfall was so extreme that it registered as a magnitude 5.2 seismic event.
The rocks and melted water suddenly swelled the rivers in the valleys below, causing torrents of water that swept buildings, bridges and earth downstream in Tibet and Nepal.

Scientists were still piecing together information from satellite and ground-level data to confirm exactly what caused the flood, but Jakob Steiner, a geoscientist at the University of Graz in Austria who is currently based in Bangladesh, said "a lower part of a glacier has really come off," noting satellite images that he said made it look "like someone cut with a huge knife through the whole lower part" of the rock and ice.
The Hindu Kush Himalayan region is warming rapidly, driving major changes in glaciers, snow cover, permafrost and mountain slopes, according to climate scientists.
Around 78% of the glacier area, located between about 14,760 and 19,685 feet above sea level, is highly exposed to warming.
"What happened yesterday is unfortunately the new normal. It's going to get worse from here onwards," Steiner said.
Americans among the missing
U.S. State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said Friday morning on Fox News that 90 Americans were among those still missing in the wake of the disaster, with five having been rescued.

In a statement, the U.S. Embassy in Nepal said the U.S. was "delivering a range of supplies requested by the Government of Nepal and is working with Nepal to ensure that assistance reaches the people who need it."

"Catholic Relief Services, working through implementing partner Caritas Nepal, will deliver more than 2.5 metric tons of food supplies, 500 blankets, 500 mosquito nets, and 500 insulating foam sheets for temporary shelter flooring to two school locations in Rasuwa," the embassy said, noting plans for subsequent supply shipments were already in place.
President Trump called the flooding terrible to see on Thursday, saying that "strong, well-built buildings were wiped out like they were toothpicks."
He told reporters in the Oval Office that U.S. officials had spoken with Nepalese leaders and offered to provide "anything they want."

Leslie Crespi, a community liaison for the Isha Foundation, a volunteer-run group that promotes well-being founded by Indian spiritual leader Sadhguru Vasudev, told CBS News about 80 people who were taking part in a pilgrimage run by the group in the region were missing.

"At this point we are awaiting word," Crespi said in a phone interview from McMinnville, Tennessee, of the missing pilgrims. "We have done as much outreach as we can through the State Department, through the embassy."

The 80 people are from 19 countries, Crespi said, including 22 from the U.S. Crespi said about 1,000 people in total were taking part in the pilgrimage. The 22 missing Americans were all adults, and included 13 women and nine men, the foundation later said in data it provided to CBS News.
She said the Isha Foundation has organized pilgrimages for 21 years, and "in those 21 years, we have never lost a life."

U.S. citizen Deepak Dandu said his wife, Sridevi Vejella, was among those missing in Nepal. She was on the pilgrimage with the Isha Foundation to Mount Kailash in Tibet — a sacred site for Hindus, Buddhists and others — which he said was a "lifelong dream" for her.
He told CBS News she was crossing from China into Nepal when the flood hit. The foundation told him she was part of a group that was present at the Gyirong Port immigration complex.
Dandu was getting ready to board a flight to Hyderabad, India, to join his son.
"He is going through a lot, hearing all the news," Dandu said of his son. "I think he is really upset. I'm trying to go there and be with him."
"10 or so seconds saved some of us"

Videos of Wednesday's disaster showed floodwaters destroying buildings, bridges and vehicles as people ran in front of the stories-high torrent. In the aftermath, broken concrete lay upended in expanses of brown mud that also caked buildings and buried streets.

Customs officer Karbir Gaire was among the survivors in Timure, the closest Nepalese village to the border with China. Gaire reached his office around 8 a.m. Wednesday and was busy working on his computer when he first felt the ground shake.

"Right after the shake, I noticed a black storm coming towards us," he recalled from Kathmandu, where he was back with family. "We all immediately started running out and within a few seconds, we were climbing uphill on the opposite side of our office building. I think those 10 or so seconds saved some of us."

Gaire said he didn't remember exactly how many people were in the office when the disaster struck, but his 15 colleagues were missing. "It was like a Hollywood movie scene. I don't call it a flood, it was a tsunami."
He described Timure as a vibrant place filled with government offices, hotels, cafes, banks, primary schools, tea shops and residential buildings, where more than 1,500 people were living.

Anjana Raja and Pattabiraman Venkatesan, a couple from the San Francisco Bay Area who were on a pilgrimage to Tibet, told CBS News in an interview Friday that they had just passed Timure headed to the border when what looked like a tsunami struck Wednesday while they were in their tour bus.

"It's like 60, 70 feet, it looked like a tsunami, but dark black," Venkatesan said. "... I could see this monster thing coming down. At that point I didn't know if it was water. I thought it was fire, forest fire, honestly."
The couple made it out of the bus and ran for higher ground.
"Along the way, you know, houses were coming down, it was bringing down homes," Venkatesan said.
"I knew I was going to die," Anjana Raja said. "I knew I was going to die."
They eventually climbed their way to a mountaintop, where they spent the night in a goat shed with other survivors, and were airlifted out the following day.
"The fact that we survived is nothing short of a miracle," Venkatesan said.

title: ‘Wheel of Fortune’ announcer Jim Thornton suspended as Sony investigates allegations
summary: Sony Pictures Television Studios says it is recasting the "Wheel of Fortune" announcer role as an investigation into Jim Thornton's conduct continues.
story: As a former player himself, the host told Fox News Digital he has 'so much empathy' for the contestants.
"Wheel of Fortune" announcer Jim Thornton has been suspended.

"We have recently been made aware of allegations concerning Jim Thornton. He has been suspended from Wheel of Fortune, and we are recasting while we conduct a thorough investigation," a spokesperson for Sony Pictures Television Studios told Fox News Digital.
Thornton was hired as an announcer for the game show in 2011.

The alleged incident was related to an American Airlines flight Thornton took in May, according to TMZ, in which another passenger complained about Thornton’s behavior. He was met by law enforcement at the gate.
TONY ROMO HIT WITH SEVERAL NEW CITATIONS AFTER OWI ARREST, FURTHER JEOPARDIZING RETURN TO NFL BROADCASTS
Jim Thornton has been the announcer of "Wheel of Fortune" since 2011. (Disney via Getty Images)
"On May 14, American Airlines Flight 1276 was met by law enforcement upon arrival at Los Angeles International Airport following concerns reported by a customer onboard," the airline told TMZ.
Thornton was not taken into custody, TMZ reported.
Fox News Digital has reached out to the airline for comment.
Thornton replaced iconic "Wheel of Fortune" announcer Charlie O’Donnell after O’Donnell's death in 2010.
Ryan Seacrest hosting "Celebrity Wheel of Fortune" last year. (Disney via Getty Images)
BOB BARKER ALLEGATIONS IN EXPLOSIVE DOCUSERIES WERE 'TRUE AND THEN SOME,' FORMER GAME SHOW HOST SAYS
Before joining "Wheel of Fortune" and "Celebrity Wheel of Fortune," he did voices for shows like "Celebrity Death Match," "The Cleveland Show" and Pixar’s "Monsters, Inc."
He has also worked on "The Price is Right" and "Jeopardy!" And he’s worked for KNX 1070 Newsradio since 1985.
Ryan Seacrest and Vanna White on "Celebrity Wheel of Fortune." (Disney via Getty Images)

Thornton has received numerous awards during his career, including the Edward R. Murrow award and an Emmy, according to his "Wheel of Fortune" biography.

title: Ed Sheeran concert workers hospitalized after forklift incident in Detroit: report
summary: A forklift accident during Ed Sheeran's concert load-out at Ford Field in Detroit injured six workers after equipment reportedly "lost control" near a tunnel.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Six people were injured Saturday during the load-out process after Ed Sheeran's concert at Ford Field in Detroit.
The Detroit Fire Department responded to a "forklift injury accident" at the stadium around 11 p.m., according to Click On Detroit.

title: Jennifer Aniston’s boyfriend, Jim Curtis, reveals what 'Friends' star is really like behind closed doors
summary: Wellness coach Jim Curtis opened up on a podcast about Jennifer Aniston's private, loving nature and the relationship tools the couple relies on.
story: The ‘Friends’ actress is one of several stars featured in Sarah Ditum's book, ‘Toxic: Women, Fame, and the Tabloid 2000s.’
Jennifer Aniston’s boyfriend, Jim Curtis, is offering a rare glimpse into their relationship, from how they handle disagreements to what the actress is really like behind closed doors.
Curtis, a wellness coach and author, opened up about his romance with the "Friends" star, revealing that their relationship is going strong.
"It's going really well. My experience of her is so grounded and so open and caring and kind and loving," he gushed during a recent appearance on "The Jamie Kern Lima Show" podcast.
JENNIFER ANISTON'S BOYFRIEND FLAUNTS STEAMY ROMANCE IN RARE PDA-PACKED PHOTOS
Jennifer Aniston’s boyfriend, Jim Curtis, reveals how the star stayed true to roots despite fame. (Getty Images, Jim Curtis Instagram)

The couple, who have been linked for more than a year, have largely kept their relationship private. But Curtis offered a candid look at their life together, including how they handle disagreements and what it means to be welcomed into Aniston’s close-knit inner circle.
"She uses words like ‘my love.’ … She has this group of best friends that are like family," he said.
"I feel incredibly blessed to be part and welcomed into that family, and I feel blessed to be in a relationship with someone that is so open-hearted."
Curtis also praised Aniston for staying grounded despite her fame.
JENNIFER ANISTON OFFERS RARE PEEK INTO HOLIDAY CELEBRATIONS WITH BOYFRIEND JIM CURTIS
Jim Curtis and Jennifer Aniston attend Elle's 2025 Women in Hollywood Celebration presented by Ralph Lauren and Bvlgari. (Michael Kovac/Getty Images for Elle)
"Inclusive. Isn't that a beautiful thing? We're really a model for how we can all be in this world, right?" Curtis said.
He said Aniston stands out because she stays true to herself despite her Hollywood fame.

"She has an opportunity. Like, you would understand if she was less so. … Right? I think that she is a real example of stepping into possibility, as she came from ... living in New York and New Jersey, and, like, there was … this kind of household name and retained herself."
Curtis also got candid about what happens when the couple disagrees.
JASON ALDEAN SAYS HE AND WIFE BRITTANY ‘AGREE TO DISAGREE’ AFTER 11 YEARS OF MARRIAGE AS THEY TEAM UP FOR DUET
Jim Curtis appears during an interview on "The Jamie Kern Lima Show." (The Jamie Kern Lima Show)
The pair, he revealed, lean on relationship tools such as communication, acceptance and understanding instead of letting disagreements escalate.
"We do a lot of meditation. We do a lot of talk," Curtis said.
He explained that because the relationship is still relatively new, they don't necessarily need heavy resolution techniques.

"And, you know … in a honeymoon phase … your tools don't have to be like big sledgehammers."

story: The "Knot’s Landing" star tells Fox News Digital she agreed to pose for Playboy only if she stayed covered.
Carmen Electra chose a bold outfit to enjoy the most important meal of the day.
In a recent Instagram post, the 54-year-old actress and model left little to the imagination when she shared photos from her "breakfast in berlin 🍓🍌."
One of the photos shows the "Epic Movie" star standing near the breakfast table on her balcony in blue lingerie worn over it featuring adjustable drawstring ties hanging from each hip.
She paired the look with a matching blue bra, which she cheekily pulled down in one photo and posed with slices of pineapples cleverly placed in front of her chest.
Electra enjoyed a breakfast of berries and other fruits. (Carmen Electra Instagram)
CARMEN ELECTRA CHANNELS HER PLAYBOY PAST IN LEOPARD-PRINT BUNNY COSTUME ON THE RED CARPET
In another photo, Electra is seen sitting down to eat in her bold breakfast attire, opting for various fruits, including berries, grapes, melons and Coca-Cola.
"Still the most gorgeous ❤️❤️" one fan wrote in the comments section, while another added, "wtf🤔shes geting younger?🔥👍❤️"
"Carm babes you look amazing!!!❤️🙌🔥" a third follower wrote and a fourth chimed in writing, "Whoa whoa whoa!! Breakfast for Champions 😎."

Electra recently made her return to Playboy after she first appeared in the pages of the magazine in 1996 when she was 24. She made her return in Playboy's Summer 2026 issue, posing in fishnets and sheer black fabric.

title: Glen Powell reveals wild night with country stars ended with beer pong at Jelly Roll’s Nashville bar
summary: Glen Powell recalls a wild Nashville night with Hardy and Dan + Shay that ended with beer pong at Jelly Roll's bar at 3 a.m. while prepping for his role.
story: Walmart is launching Glen Powell’s Smash Kitchen organic condiment line online and in stores nationwide as consumers prioritize health and wellness.
Glen Powell recalled having a wild night out in Nashville with country music royalty while preparing for his role in the upcoming movie, "The Comeback King."
In the Judd Apatow-directed comedy, the 37-year-old actor plays Aubrey King, a disgraced country star who attempts to rebuild his life and career after experiencing a dramatic downfall.

During a recent appearance on "Jimmy Kimmer Live," which was guest-hosted by Jelly Roll, Powell, who co-wrote the script with Apatow, explained how he collaborated with real-life country musicians and set out to fully immerse himself in Music City’s culture to make the project feel authentic.
JELLY ROLL ROLLS AWAY FROM APOLITICAL PAST AFTER TRUMP JOKES SPARK MAGA AND ‘SNOWFLAKE’ LABELS

"I've been a fan of country music my whole life, and I wanted to make sure that we did this right," Powell told Jelly Roll. "We made it not about country music. We wanted to make it with country music.
Glen Powell detailed having a wild night out with some of country's biggest stars in Nashville.  (Getty Images for BAFTA)
"And one of the things I did as we were, like, writing, I was like, 'Oh, I want to get the full experience of writing with Nashville,'" he remembered.
Powell recalled that he decided to team up with country singer-songwriter Hardy for a daytime writing session.
"Did y'all write, or did y'all go out drinking?" Jelly Roll joked.
"We first wrote, then we drank," Powell replied. "So, we wrote this great song. I was really excited about it. And then he's like, 'Hey man, we should go out and really hit the town.'"

Powell said he and Hardy joined his "buddies," country duo Dan + Shay, for an outing in Lower Broadway, Nashville's iconic entertainment district known for its packed honky-tonks and live country music.
The actor is playing a disgraced country music singer in the upcoming movie "The Comeback King." (Disney via Getty Images)
GLEN POWELL SHOTGUNS A BEER ON STAGE WITH COUNTRY SUPERSTAR LUKE COMBS
"All of a sudden, like, one bar turned to 12," Powell recalled.
"Oh, you went honky-tonk," Jelly Roll quipped.
JELLY ROLL UNLEASHES CRUDE JOKES ABOUT TRUMP'S WEIGHT ON 'KIMMEL', 'FROM ONE FAT PIG TO ANOTHER'
Powell remembered that, 12 stops later, the group finally landed at Jelly Roll’s Broadway establishment Goodnight in the early morning hours.
"We ended up playing beer pong there, I think, at like 3 in the morning," Powell admitted.
"Let's go!" Jelly Roll exclaimed. "You strike me as a great beer pong player. How'd you fair?"
Powell said that while he considers himself a "pretty good" player, he proved no match for Hardy.
"Hardy smoked me," he said. "I'll be honest with you."
"Hardy's an absolute rager," Jelly Roll agreed.
JELLY ROLL HID PAINFUL 'SECRET' WHILE CELEBRATING AT AWARDS SHOW
"Do you recall the first time you ever played beer pong?" the "Save Me" hitmaker asked Powell.
"First time I ever played beer pong? Oh, wow. That's a good question. Do you remember yours?" Powell asked.
"Well, I went to prison instead of college, so I missed the entire beer pong era, you know," Jelly Roll, who has been open about his past incarcerations quipped.
"You know, I missed out on the whole prison beer pong experience, but that one's not on my bucket list," Powell joked as the audience laughed.

Powell admitted losing to Hardy while playing beer pong at 3 a.m. (Disney via Getty Images)
Jelly Roll was among the country stars, including Miranda Lambert, Brad Paisley and Riley Green, who made cameos in "The Comeback King."

During his appearance on the late-night show, Powell recalled how "The Comeback King" marks the first time he has ever sung on screen. The "Top Gun: Maverick" star credited his voice coach, Eric Vitro; his experience singing with his mother in nursing homes; and his sister Leslie for guiding him through the vocal preparation.

Powell noted that Leslie, an accomplished singer-songwriter, "wrote a lot of music" for the movie. Leslie previously contributed music to some of Powell's other projects, including "Anyone But You," "Twisters" and "Set It Up."
The actor performed all of his own songs in the movie.  (Arturo Holmes/Getty Images)

title: Luke Bryan threatens to 'knock the s--- out of' online trolls trashing his new song
summary: Luke Bryan told Theo Von he'd confront trolls who accused his "Fish Hunt Golf Drink" song of being AI-generated, calling out teenage critics online.
story: The ‘American Idol’ judge explained how his upbringing impacted his life
Luke Bryan has a bone to pick with his haters.

During an appearance on the "This Past Weekend with Theo Von" podcast, the "American Idol" judge and country star opened up about the backlash surrounding his latest song, "Fish Hunt Golf Drink," which some social media users accused of being created with artificial intelligence.
Bryan said the controversy began with a "narrative" created and amplified online.
LUKE BRYAN CREDITS RELIGIOUS ROOTS AND SMALL-TOWN VALUES FOR HELPING HIM NAVIGATE A ‘CHALLENGING LIFE’
Luke Bryan opened up about the controversy surrounding his latest song.  (Getty Images for ACM)

"That’s the crazy thing about where we’re at with social [media]," he said. "They started a narrative that we AI-ed it. And now, whether you like the song or not, or whether you like me as an artist, whether you like what I'm about or whatever … now I'm the guy that somebody said that I AI-ed a song and wrote it.
"You get one or two kids with a bunch of Instagram, a bunch of followers, that say we AI-ed it, and then the whole world goes on their narrative."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Von argued that he doesn't think people actually believe he used AI to create the song, but Bryan said the backlash has been "pretty crazy," and he recalled seeing posts from people who told him they hated him.
"And they’re like at a camera going, ‘I hate you.’ … And I’m like, ‘I can see your face. If I see you one day, I’m going to f---ing knock the s--- out of you, dude,’" he said.
However, Bryan acknowledged that many of the online comments were coming from teenagers.
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
The country star refuted claims he used artificial intelligence to write "Fish Hunt Golf Drink." (Terry Wyatt/WireImage)

"But then I’m like, ‘Well, wait.’ I’m not sure I’m happy about a bunch of teenagers telling a 50-year-old man he’s a piece of s--- songwriter," he said. "And then I’m like, ‘Dude, you’re 16. You’re talking to a grown man who’s made a s--- ton of money doing this.'
"It’s just so far out there," he added. "I’m like, if I caught my kids doing some stuff like that, I would kill them."
Earlier this year, Bryan addressed the AI accusations shortly after the song's release.
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
"We’ve had some negativity out there. Some trolls kind of saying that I ‘AI-ed’ it, which is completely false," he told NBC4 at the Memorial Pro-Am on June 3.
"That song was designed for one thing," he added. "To have fun and tell the world what I love to do and what I strive to do."
Bryan said he'd come down hard on his kids if they acted the way some teenagers online are acting toward him.  (The Mega Agency)
Songwriters Chase McGill and Matt Dragstrem also shut down the false narrative during an interview with Rolling Stone.

"[Bryan] is the least artificial person I’ve ever met," McGill said. "The only way I’ve actually succeeded in country music, ever, is by sitting in the room with good friends and enjoying making the song up that day. I don’t believe that I would feel any fulfillment from saying, ‘AI, write me a song about whatever.’ That’s not what I signed up for."
The idea behind the song came up organically, said McGill.

"Luke was texting one of his buddies, and the guy was like, ‘Let’s hang soon,’" he said. "Luke sent him an emoji of a fish, an emoji of a deer, an emoji of a golf club and a beer emoji, and said, ‘You pick which one.’ Then he showed it to us. He was like, ‘Dude, this could be a cool song.’

title: Dick Van Dyke shocks fans by posting inversion table workout at age 100
summary: Dick Van Dyke, 100, shared a video of his inversion table workout on Instagram, proving his lifelong commitment to fitness is still going strong.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
When it comes to his fitness, Dick Van Dyke is not slowing down anytime soon.
On Friday, Van Dyke, 100, shared a video of himself stretching on an inversion table.
"#DVD100 1/2 workout inversion table #keepmoving," he captioned the clip, which he shared on Instagram on Friday, Aug. 28.
‘A MAN WITHOUT LOVE’ SINGER ENGELBERT HUMPERDINCK CREDITS UNDERWATER WORKOUT FOR KEEPING HIM ‘ALIVE’ AT 90
Dick Van Dyke is still prioritizing his fitness at 100 years old. (Getty Images)
Fans took to the comments section to gush about the actor and his athletic skills.
"I love this, let's all work out with DVD! We need you in this world and it makes me happy to see you!" one fan wrote, while another said: "Thank goodness you're doing amazing. Stay healthy."

Other comments from fans include: "He's showing all of us what we could be doing. I'm not of course," "Stretching will definitely help you stay in your best shape," "Truly amazing and inspirational," "This is why you're going to outlive us all and I'm happy to be here for it."

Last year, Van Dyke wrote an essay for The Times U.K., which described how staying active has been key to keeping himself physically strong and mentally sharp.

"I still try to hit the gym three times a week," he explained. "I don’t know why this is something I still want to do, but it is. I’m not a ‘wake up and go back to bed’ type just yet, unless it’s cold and rainy. If I miss too many gym days, I really can feel it — a stiffness creeping in here and there. Dick Van Dyke will turn 101 years old in December.  (Gilbert Flores/Variety via Getty Images)

"The secret ingredient is the music," he continued. "Most of my humming and singing really happens when I’m going from one machine to another. By ‘going’ I mean dancing. You heard me — dancing! And if I’m really feeling it, I’m no quiet warbler; I’m a Broadway belter."

title: Sarah Ferguson plots bold return to Britain after Epstein scandal shattered reputation: expert
summary: Sarah Ferguson is reportedly lined up for a tell-all TV documentary to share her side of the story after the damaging Jeffrey Epstein emails, according to royal experts.
story: Andrew Lownie, author of "Entitled," weighs in on former Prince Andrew and Sarah Ferguson’s evolving relationship amid royal scrutiny. The exes were once known as the "happiest divorced couple."
Sarah Ferguson has made a career out of comebacks — and after seven months largely hidden from public view, the former Duchess of York may be preparing for another.
Ferguson, 66, may be ready to step back into the spotlight, with one royal commentator describing the former Duchess of York as a "chameleon" who has repeatedly managed to reinvent herself.
"Sarah Ferguson is forever the chameleon," British broadcaster and photographer Helena Chard told Fox News Digital. "She always seems to bounce back."
SARAH FERGUSON IS HOPING 'TO EVAPORATE LIKE MIST' AS SHE'S SEEN FOR THE FIRST TIME IN 7 MONTHS: EXPERT
Sarah Ferguson is reportedly preparing to return to public life after spending seven months largely out of the spotlight. (Rob Kim/Getty Images for Global Citizen)
"The one person who believes in Sarah is Sarah!" Chard added.

One element of Ferguson's reported fresh start could be a new home in Britain. Chard said she understands Ferguson will be based in the Home Counties in a "£10,000 a month plush gated property with granny annex."
But a new residence may only be part of the attempted reset.
Chard said Ferguson has attracted interest from television producers and could use a documentary or interview to put forward her version of events.

"Sarah has admittedly made some silly decisions. However, it's reported that she is lined up to appear in a TV documentary when settled in Britain," Chard said. However, she is considering working on her own programme to retain control."
FORMER PRINCE ANDREW FACES WIDENING MISCONDUCT PROBE AS POLICE LAUNCH WITNESS HUNT

Sarah Ferguson is said to be planning a fresh start in Britain while considering television opportunities that could allow Sarah Ferguson to tell her side of the story. (Stephane Cardinale - Corbis/Corbis via Getty Images)

After Andrew lost his royal titles in October 2025 and was forced to vacate Royal Lodge, Ferguson also had to find somewhere else to live. The former Duchess of York has reportedly been spending her time abroad. Ferguson had been staying at a chalet in the Austrian Alps, People reported.

title: Big & Rich say Dolly Parton put fame aside to help neighbors after 2016 Tennessee wildfires
summary: Big & Rich recall Dolly Parton's heartfelt response to the 2016 Gatlinburg wildfires and her "Smoky Mountains Rise" telethon that raised millions.
story: Big & Rich’s John Rich remembers seeing a different side of Dolly Parton during her 2016 wildfire relief efforts, saying she wasn’t a world-famous icon that day, but "a country girl who was trying to help out her neighbors."
Big & Rich saw firsthand how Dolly Parton put her fame aside after the 2016 Tennessee wildfires that devastated the community.

During an interview with Fox News Digital, the country music duo, Big Kenny and John Rich, who recently released their protest single titled "Hello AI," recalled seeing Parton be an "extraordinary person" for her community and trying to help her neighbors.

"One thing that struck me that particular day, you know, Gatlinburg had basically burned to the ground. And that's right in her backyard, where she's from," Rich began. "So, she was distraught over what was going on. In the moment of those performances, it wasn't like you were standing next to Dolly Parton, the world-famous iconic singer. You were standing next to a country girl who was trying to help out her neighbors. That was really her whole point."
Big & Rich recalled Dolly Parton putting fame aside after the 2016 Tennessee wildfires. (Getty Images)

After devastating wildfires tore through Gatlinburg and Sevier County in November 2016, Parton rallied the country music community to help her native East Tennessee. Parton hosted the star-studded "Smoky Mountains Rise: A Benefit for the My People Fund" telethon on Dec. 13, with Big & Rich among the nearly 20 artists who performed.
DOLLY PARTON'S LIFE IN HER OWN WORDS: FROM SMOKY MOUNTAINS POVERTY TO COUNTRY MUSIC IMMORTALITY

The benefit ultimately raised more than $9 million for wildfire victims after the fires killed 14 people and damaged or destroyed more than 2,400 buildings, according to ABC News. The money supported Parton’s My People Fund, which provided direct financial assistance to families who lost their homes.

Big Kenny recalled not only the "Smoky Mountains Rise" performance with Parton, but every encounter with the late country music legend during their interview with Fox News Digital.
John Rich of Big & Rich in 2018. (Johnny Louis/Getty Images)

"There have been multiple interactions over the years with Dolly and one thing you absolutely know about her is that she's a big-hearted and a super kind person. And that's how I would describe her that day. You could tell that, you know, it just meant the world to her to be doing what she was doing, and it meant the world to her that we showed up that day to help her out," he said.
DOLLY PARTON'S BELOVED LITERACY MISSION SEES SURGE OF SUPPORT AFTER COUNTRY ICON'S DEATH

Big Kenny continued, "And every other time I've ever run into her, she's just a super sweet and kind and funny and smart and just every other kind of adjective you can use for an extraordinary human being like Dolly Parton."

title: Meghan Markle’s UK return poses Palace control ‘nightmare,’ expert warns
summary: Meghan Markle's U.K. return means Buckingham Palace can't control her projects, but experts say the institution still holds leverage over royal access.
story: Fox News correspondent Natalie Chuck has the latest on Prince Harry, Meghan Markle and family officially moving back to the U.K. on The Story.
Meghan Markle is returning to Britain with more independence than she had as a working royal, an arrangement experts say could test Buckingham Palace's boundaries.

Markle, 45, and Prince Harry, 41, recently relocated to the United Kingdom with their children Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5, for an extended stay though they will remain private, non-working members of the royal family.

While the couple is expected to establish a private residence outside London and keep their home in Montecito, California, royal observers told Fox News Digital that Markle's ability to pursue her own media, business and public-facing projects from Britain could create new tension with the institution she once represented.
PRINCE HARRY, MEGHAN MARKLE PLANNING TO MOVE BACK TO UK WITH CHILDREN 6 YEARS AFTER ROYAL EXIT: REPORTS

"The nightmare for the Palace is that they can’t be controlled," royal commentator Richard Fitzwilliams told Fox News Digital. "Diary clashes will probably mean royal engagements are overshadowed by what the Sussexes choose to do and what they are, or are not, asked to by the Palace."
Meghan Markle and Prince Harry's return to the U.K. could create a "nightmare" for Buckingham Palace, according to a royal expert. (Getty Images)

Kinsey Schofield, host of YouTube’s "Kinsey Schofield Unfiltered," said that Buckingham Palace will have "very little control" over the Duke and Duchess of Sussex's public and commercial activities because they no longer represent Harry's father King Charles as working royals.
PRINCE HARRY'S MOST CONTROVERSIAL ROYAL PLAN COULD STILL BECOME REALITY, AUTHOR SAYS
"They are private citizens and no longer working on behalf of the King, so Buckingham Palace isn’t approving Meghan’s interviews, appearances, Instagram posts or commercial projects," Schofield said.

"But Harry is still the King’s son and Meghan is still the Duchess of Sussex, so there is an inevitable association with the monarchy," she added. "That’s the complicated part. They can operate independently while still benefiting from an enormous amount of public interest that exists because of Harry’s DNA."
The couple moved back to Britain with their children for an extended stay. (Justin Goff Photos/Getty Images)
MEGHAN MARKLE’S ROYAL EXIT HAD WARNING SIGNS YEARS EARLIER, VETERAN CORRESPONDENT REVEALS

Markle's status as a private citizen living in the U.K. marks a sharp departure from her life as a working royal, when Palace protocols and communications staff shaped much of her public role. The former "Suits" star is returning with her own career, team and support system, according to People magazine.

"She has been vocal about how she felt about it before, but that doesn’t mean things are going to be exactly the same again," an ally told People. "It doesn’t mean it can’t be different and can’t change."
Another source told the outlet that the Sussexes' support network is "stronger now than it ever was to protect her — to protect them."
However, Schofield pointed out that Buckingham Palace retains one important source of influence.
KING CHARLES SENDS 'DEFIANCE' MESSAGE TO PRINCE WILLIAM WITH BUCKINGHAM PALACE ROOM OFFER TO HARRY: EXPERT

"The palace can’t control what they do, but it can control access to the institution. It can decide how much proximity they have to working royals, royal residences, and official events," she said. "That is where the palace still has considerable leverage."
"Meghan may be returning without palace restrictions, but she is also returning without palace protection," she added. "You don’t get one without losing the other."
PRINCE HARRY, MEGHAN MARKLE BLASTED FOR ‘FAUX ROYAL TOUR’ AS EXPERTS ACCUSE COUPLE OF EXPLOITING TITLES

However, Buckingham Palace's ability to limit the Sussexes’ access to official royal events, however, would not prevent their public appearances, announcements or business ventures from drawing attention away from the working royals. Fitzwilliams said that dynamic could become particularly challenging when it comes to the carefully coordinated royal calendar.
"The problem is that royal diaries are planned well in advance," Fitzwilliams said. "Here there are likely to be numerous clashes, and this will fuel fascination with the Sussexes."
Markle and Harry will not be resuming their roles as working royals. (Chris Jackson/Getty Images)
PRINCE WILLIAM LIKELY 'LIVID' OVER MEGHAN MARKLE'S 'TASTELESS' PHOTOS AT PRINCESS DIANA'S HOME: EXPERT

Schofield told Fox News Digital that a competing announcement would not necessarily violate a formal Palace rule, but she noted there are longstanding expectations around the timing of public engagements.

"If Meghan were repeatedly scheduling appearances or announcements to coincide with major royal engagements, people would notice," she said. "She might not be breaking a written rule, but there are conventions and courtesies around these things."
PRINCE WILLIAM'S ABSENCE SPEAKS VOLUMES AS KING CHARLES REUNITES WITH PRINCE HARRY AND MEGHAN MARKLE: EXPERTS
"If you consistently attempt to overshadow the working Royal Family, eventually the pattern becomes the story," Schofield added.
Schofield explained that the concern over competing headlines echoes the central issue Queen Elizabeth II confronted when Harry and Markle stepped back from their roles as working royals in 2020.

At the time, the late queen rejected a proposed hybrid arrangement that would have allowed the couple to pursue financial independence while continuing to carry out official duties and retain the benefits of their royal connection.

"This is essentially the dilemma the late Queen was trying to avoid with the original ‘half-in, half-out’ rejection," Schofield said. "Meghan can enjoy enormous interest because she married into the Royal Family without having to behave or work like a royal."

"But there is another side to that bargain," she continued. "She doesn’t have the institution behind her anymore either. There is no royal communications operation required to defend her, no royal security, and no guaranteed place at major royal occasions. A lot of the perks are gone."
Royal experts warned that the duo's activities may clash with official royal engagements. (Chris Jackson - Pool/Getty Images)

The experts agreed that the question of access is further complicated by the fractured relationship between the Sussexes and the royal family. The couple publicly detailed strains within the royal family in their 2021 interview with Oprah Winfrey, their 2022 Netflix docuseries "Harry & Meghan" and Harry’s bombshell 2023 memoir "Spare."
Schofield said that history could make Palace staff particularly wary as Harry and Markle establish a new life in the U.K.

"There is also a significant trust deficit," she said. "Harry published private family conversations in ‘Spare,’ and Harry and Meghan have discussed private royal relationships publicly in interviews and their Netflix series. That history doesn’t disappear simply because they’re living in Britain again."

British broadcaster Helena Chard told Fox News Digital that Charles and his son and heir Prince William may need to establish clearer expectations around the Sussexes’ access to official engagements and the working royal family as they settle back into Britain.
"Formalities need to be drawn up, put in place and made clear to all," Chard said. "These will essentially be the 'dos and don'ts' formalities."
One expert said that Charles and William may have to set boundaries regarding the couple's access to official engagements and the working royal family. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)

According to People magazine, the Sussexes' move back to the U.K. is also about more than their business interests or public profiles. title: Debi Mazar says 'Entourage' set 'got toxic' after she returned from having her second daughter
summary: Debi Mazar says the "Entourage" set became "toxic" and she felt judged for her weight after returning to the HBO show after having her second daughter.
story: The former ‘Boy Meets World’ actress turned adult film star stars in an episode of ‘Hollywood Demons’
"Entourage" star Debi Mazar is opening up about what she described as a difficult experience on the set of the hit show.

The actress, who played no-nonsense publicist Shauna Roberts throughout the HBO show’s eight-season run, reflected on her experience in a recent interview with The Sunday Times, calling the first season a "joy-fest" before saying the atmosphere shifted.
"In the third season, the set was a testosterone-fueled environment," Mazar told the outlet. "I’m tough, but it got toxic towards the end for me."
JACK OSBOURNE FIRES BACK AT BODY SHAMERS CALLING HIM 'GROSSLY UNDERWEIGHT'
"Entourage" star Debi Mazar opened up about her experience on the set of the hit show. (Getty Images)
Mazar, 62, said she returned to work after welcoming her second daughter and felt judged over her appearance.
"They didn’t like that I got fat, even though I got skinny again," she said.

The "Goodfellas" star said the situation was complicated in part because she has never been one to keep quiet about how she feels. Still, Mazar stressed that she remained professional and was grateful for her time on the series.
Mazar — with Jerry Ferrara, Adrian Grenier, Jeremy Piven, Kevin Connolly and Kevin Dillon — played Shauna Roberts throughout the HBO show’s eight-season run, from 2004 to 2011. (FilmMagic)
"It was a lot of fun, until it wasn’t," she said.
Fox News Digital reached out to HBO for comment.

"Entourage," which followed the highs and pitfalls of a rising actor navigating Hollywood with his childhood friends, ran on HBO from 2004 to 2011. Mazar reprised her role as Shauna in the 2015 movie based on the series.

Mazar is among several stars who have recently opened up about their "toxic" experiences on Hollywood sets.
Earlier this year, Rose McGowan said Hollywood executives openly obsessed over her fluctuating weight during her stint on "Charmed" in the early 2000s.
Rose McGowan previously opened up about what she experienced on the "Charmed" set. (Getty Images)
During an appearance on the "We Need to Talk" podcast, McGowan — who joined the cast in 2001 — recalled how show executives would often mull over her weight gain or loss.
"They would circle around me to check my weight when I came back from season to season," she said, referencing show producers. "I think it was just really inspecting their product."
BELLA THORNE SAYS HOLLYWOOD TREATED HER LIKE A KID ON SCREEN AND AN ADULT OFF CAMERA
"There was no chill with it. It was completely fine to be that way," she added. "Now they have to kind of pay lip service to being different."

Danielle Fishel — who famously portrayed Topanga Lawrence in the beloved '90s series "Boy Meets World" — has been open about facing significant body-image struggles during the height of the show's success.
"Boy Meets World" star Danielle Fishel says she felt body-shamed during a period of time while filming the beloved sitcom. (Valerie Macon/AFP via Getty Images)

"I was aware, even if nobody said it to me directly... that as far as the people in power were concerned, my body was a problem," Fishel, 44, said in an April interview with Us Weekly. "I remember around the time of [1998’s] prom episode being aware that they didn’t want me wearing something sleeveless."
Toward the end of the series, Fishel felt she was "no longer attractive" because she had put on weight.

During the show's last season, Fishel's weight gain was addressed in an episode titled, "She's Having My Baby Back Ribs." In the episode, Topanga pretends to be pregnant as she struggles with body insecurities.

title: Melinda French Gates stuns festival crowd, pledges to match Olivia Rodrigo's fundraising for $20M haul
summary: Melinda French Gates pledged to match every donation at Olivia Rodrigo's Daisy Chain Fields festival, doubling the fundraising total to $20 million.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Olivia Rodrigo introduced Daisy Chain Fields festival attendees to a surprise guest with a huge heart.
After revealing that her inaugural music festival raised $10 million for various women-focused nonprofits, the "drivers license" singer revealed a shocking fundraising update.
Before her headlining set at the event in Irvine, Rodrigo announced that Melinda French Gates would match every donation to the dollar, for a grand total of $20 million fundraised.
Olivia Rodrigo introduced Melinda French Gates at her inaugural Daisy Chain Fields festival on Saturday in Irvine, Calif. (Monica Schipper)

Rodrigo, who announced her first female-driven festival in June, told the crowd that she was "grateful" for each of the booked acts who performed "for free" throughout the day as she celebrated her initial $10 million fundraising effort.

"I really believe that giving women the tools to decide their own futures and live healthy lives free of violence and discrimination is the most effective tool we have at changing the world for the better," Rodrigo said. "And I don’t know many people who represent that idea more than Melinda French Gates."

The former Disney Channel actress admitted that Gates was "one of the most inspiring women I've ever met," while championing her dedication to "empowering women and girls that might have otherwise been forgotten."
Gates matched fundraising efforts Saturday with a grand total of $20 million raised for women-driven organizations. (Christopher Polk)

"She's generous and brave and has done so much good in this world, and I’m totally floored because, as well as being in attendance here tonight, she’s pledged to double every dollar that we made here today to a grand total of funds being donated to $20 million," Rodrigo told the crowd. "I'm so grateful!"
"Look at what you have done," Gates told Rodrigo after joining the "good 4 u" singer on stage. "Look at what you created!"

"What I love about you is that you know that real power is not up here on stage, it's with everybody there, all of you," Gates continued. "When women and girls come together to dream and to lead, we change the world."
Olivia Rodrigo admitted that Sarah McLachlan inspired her to create Daisy Chain Fields after McLachlan's success with Lilith Fair. (Kayla Bartkowski)

The former wife of Microsoft founder Bill Gates added, "And, so long after the lights go down from this festival, the organizations doing this work will keep doing it because you all are here, so thank you for being here and thank you, Olivia."
During a press conference Friday before the festival, Rodrigo announced the multi-million figure raised for specific, women-focused nonprofits.

Ten organizations will receive an equally split total from the funds raised at the festival, which included: Baby2Baby, Black Mamas Matter Alliance, Center for Reproductive Rights, FreeFrom, Jhpiego, Johns Hopkins Center for Indigenous Health, National Domestic Workers Alliance, National Institute for Reproductive Health, National Women’s Law Center and Planned Parenthood.

title: Queen Camilla puts past differences with Prince Harry aside as King Charles seeks closer family ties: experts
summary: Queen Camilla reportedly offered Prince Harry tea with a "fixed smile" at the secret Highgrove House meeting ahead of the Sussexes moving to the U.K. prioritizing King Charles III's welfare.
story: Why did King Charles ultimately choose Queen Camilla? Catherine Mayer, author of "Divide & Rule," breaks down the unlikely love story that changed the monarchy.
Queen Camilla will put King Charles III first as the royal family navigates Prince Harry’s return to the U.K., royal experts told Fox News Digital.
The Duke and Duchess of Sussex returned to the U.K. on Aug. 26. Their children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet, will begin school in Britain in September.

Royal experts believe the king, who is still receiving treatment for an undisclosed form of cancer, wants a relationship with his grandchildren. Camilla, they said, is prepared to support her husband as Harry hopes for reconciliation with his family.
PRINCE HARRY, MEGHAN MARKLE’S UK MOVE PUTS FRESH SPOTLIGHT ON THEIR EXPLOSIVE CLAIMS AGAINST ROYAL FAMILY
Prince Harry and his family returned to the U.K. on August 26. (Isabel Infantes//POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

Before the Sussexes’ return, the king met with Harry, Meghan and their children at Highgrove House on July 10. Vanity Fair royal correspondent Katie Nicholl later reported that, according to sources, "not even the Prince and Princess of Wales were made aware that the meeting was taking place." Camilla was present.

"Camilla has weathered far bigger storms than the Sussexes’ 2020 move, or Prince Harry’s book, ‘Spare,’" royal commentator Meredith Constant told Fox News Digital. "Camilla knows how to lie low when she needs to. She’s going to go through the motions and put on a good face for her husband as he works on his relationship with his younger son."
Camilla and Prince Harry stand on the balcony of Buckingham Palace during Trooping the Colour on June 13, 2015, in London, England. (Getty Images)

"While Prince William and King Charles are not in lockstep over how to handle Prince Harry’s return, they understand that they are a unit with their respective wives," she said. "William wouldn’t expect Camilla to take a stand against her husband anymore than Charles would expect that of Kate."
WATCH: WHY KING CHARLES ALWAYS CAME BACK TO QUEEN CAMILLA: AUTHOR

Royal biographer Tom Bower told the Daily Mail that Camilla approached her stepson with what InStyle magazine described as "an olive branch" — a "fixed smile" before she "offered him tea." A source told Bower the meeting was "polite with no recrimination."

"Albeit this was indeed a polite gesture, it was merely a tiny aperture being opened, not a welcome for any full return as senior royals at all," British royal expert Hilary Fordwich told Fox News Digital. "It’s traditionally British to offer tea as merely a polite gesture. Camilla is dedicated to the king’s health and welfare, so it’s not surprising."

From left: Prince William, Prince of Wales, King Charles III and Queen Camilla attend the Thistle Service at St. Giles' Cathedral in Edinburgh, Scotland on July 1, 2026. (Aaron Chown/POOL/AFP via Getty Images)
Royal historian Catherine Mayer told People magazine that Camilla "is a non-negotiable part of Charles’ life," adding, "there’s no reconciliation with [the king] without her."
Queen Camilla shelters under a parasol during a visit to Penguin Beach at London Zoo in London, ahead of meeting Prince Harry and his family on July 10, 2026. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)

The road to reconciliation may be a lengthy one for Harry. The Duke and Duchess of Sussex stepped back as senior royals in 2020, saying they faced intense scrutiny from the British press and lacked support from the palace.

After moving to California, the couple aired their grievances in interviews and documentaries. Harry’s 2023 memoir, "Spare," further strained his relationship with his family. Royal experts previously told Fox News Digital that Harry and his older brother, Prince William, haven’t spoken since 2022.
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, relocated to California in 2020. (Chris Jackson/Getty Images)
After "Spare" was published in 2023, Harry accused his stepmother of leaking private conversations to the media to burnish her reputation.
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
Prince Harry's book "Spare" is displayed in a bookstore on Dec. 16, 2023, in Bath, England. (Matt Cardy/Getty Images)

In interviews, Harry accused family members of getting "into bed with the devil" to gain favorable tabloid coverage. He singled out Camilla's efforts to rehabilitate her image with the British public after her long-running relationship with his father.
Camilla, who once faced widespread public criticism, eventually won over many royal watchers through her charitable work and support of the king. Charles was crowned in 2023.

Britain's Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex, looks on as Britain's King Charles III leaves Westminster Abbey after the coronation ceremonies in central London on May 6, 2023. He was sitting a few rows away from his family. (Ben Stansall/POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

"Yes, she was hurt by Harry’s unkind words," British broadcaster and photographer Helena Chard told Fox News Digital. "However, she is made of tough stuff and plays a vital role as King Charles’ steadfast partner, prioritizing his protection. Supporting the king through rigorous treatment and applauding his determination, Camilla’s desire is to ensure her husband’s [golden] years bring him peace, health and joy."
Prince Harry and Camilla at St. George's Chapel in Windsor, England, on May 17, 2008. (WireImage/Getty)

"There is the fleeting thought that, despite Harry’s series of cutting jibes, Queen Camilla is reminded of a sad young Harry," she said. "She is sympathetic to Harry’s deep-rooted problems. But their relationship is tricky."
In 2023, Harry told "Good Morning America" that he and Camilla "haven’t spoken for a long time."

Prince Charles, Prince of Wales, his wife Camilla, Duchess of Cornwall, and son Prince Harry watch a flypast over The Mall from the Buckingham Palace balcony during National Commemoration Day on July 10, 2005, in London. (Getty Images)
"I love every member of my family, despite the differences," he said. "So when I see her, we’re perfectly pleasant with each other."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

King Charles, Queen Camilla and Meghan, Duchess of Sussex attend The Prince of Wales' 70th Birthday Patronage Celebration at Buckingham Palace in London, England, on May 22, 2018. (Chris Jackson/Getty Images)

"She’s my stepmother," he continued. "I don’t look at her as an evil stepmother. I see someone who married into this institution and has done everything she can to improve her own reputation and her own image, for her own sake."

In May 2025, Harry told the BBC that he wanted reconciliation, saying, "There’s no point in continuing to fight anymore" and "life is precious." At the time, the prince said, "I do not know how much longer my father has left."
Prince Harry told the BBC in 2025 that he's ready for reconciliation. (Samir Hussein/WireImage)
A source told People magazine that Harry had been thinking about the move "for a while." With Archie and Lilibet now school-age, the couple felt the timing made sense, the outlet reported.

Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex, and Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, attend the David Foster Foundation 40th Anniversary Celebration on Aug. 7, 2026, in Victoria, British Columbia. (The David Foster Foundation via Getty Images)
As for Camilla and the rest of the royal family, royal experts expect them to keep calm and carry on.

"Members of the British royal family do not cause a scene," Constant said. "If they want information out there, it will find a way to the papers. Camilla doesn’t need to say a word to get her message across. As long as her stepson isn’t interfering with her husband’s reign, it’s just business as usual."

Queen Camilla visits the Chaos and Control exhibition at the Royal Scottish Academy of Art and Architecture in Edinburgh during the bicentenary celebrations on June 30, 2026. (Steve Welsh/WPA Pool/Getty Images)
Chard said she believes Camilla is choosing to put her personal feelings aside and prioritize what is best for her husband.
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
King Charles III and Queen Camilla attend a service at Crathie Kirk Church on Aug. 23, 2026, in Crathie, Aberdeenshire. (Peter Summers/Getty Images)

"Queen Camilla raced to the July 10 meeting at Highgrove in support of her husband, not for the love of Harry," she said. "Camilla was a listening ear and offered the usual stability to her husband. Queen Camilla is interested in the best for her husband and the monarchy going forward."
But not every royal appears to be on the same page about the Sussexes.
The Duke and Duchess of Sussex at Project Healthy Minds' World Mental Health Day Festival held at Spring Studios on Oct. 9, 2025, in New York City. (Kristina Bumphrey/Variety via Getty Images)

"Prince William, to date, has still had no contact with his wayward brother," Fordwich said. "The imminent future looks rather awkward. If Harry and Meghan refrain from any public accusations, any monetization of royal contacts, and are discreet, William is likely to be more open to controlled conduct than any sort of reconciliation. Harry should take a page out of Camilla’s playbook to gain eventual trust and respect. Silence is golden."
Prince William, Prince of Wales, Duke of Rothesay and Prince George of Wales attend a service at Crathie Kirk Church on Aug. 23, 2026, in Crathie, Aberdeenshire. (Peter Summers/Getty Images)

Kensington Palace, which represents the office of the Prince and Princess of Wales, told Fox News Digital that it does not comment on personal family matters. Fox News Digital reached out to Buckingham Palace for comment.

Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex and Meghan, Duchess of Sussex are seen greeting members of the public at the Cruising Yacht Club of Australia on April 17, 2026, in Sydney, Australia. (Cameron Spencer/Getty Images)

Details about the location of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex's private, non-royal home and the children’s school are being closely guarded, People magazine reported. The outlet also reported that the king was made aware of their plans on Aug. 16 and welcomed the opportunity to see more of his son’s family "in a private and personal capacity."

title: Scott Wolf's wife says ‘my brain turned on me’ as she apologizes to family for 'profound harm' after psychosis

story: Ian Somerhalder reflected on why the people, not the spotlight, are what he misses most about Hollywood after stepping away from acting.

In an Instagram carousel, Kelley said she had been diagnosed with what she called "breakthrough drug-induced mania with psychosis," which she attributed to a combination of stress, past trauma, hormonal shifts, hallucinogens and prescribed medication.

"It’s been a year since I recognized what everyone around me could see: I was not well, and I needed help," Kelley wrote. "I felt like my brain had been hijacked, and the world was moving at the speed of a freight train."

title: Teen dies from ‘brain-eating amoeba’ just days after young girl succumbs to same rare infection
summary: A North Carolina teen's first symptom was severe headaches before a brain-eating amoeba infection proved fatal, his mother shared on GoFundMe.
story: Dr. Jeffrey Kahn, chief of pediatric infectious diseases at UT Southwestern and Children's Health in Dallas, Texas, says Naegleria fowleri is very rare, but nearly 100% fatal.
A North Carolina teenager has died from a rare and often fatal infection caused by an amoeba found in warm freshwater, state health officials said.
In a GoFundMe set up by the teen’s mother, she shared that his first symptom was "severe headaches."
"I never imagined that something like this could be so serious," she said.
BEACHGOERS WARNED AFTER DEADLY 'FLESH-EATING' BACTERIA KILLS 5 IN SOUTHERN STATE
The illness is caused by Naegleria fowleri, an amoeba (one-celled living organism) that inhabits ponds, lakes and rivers.
"We extend our condolences to the family, friends and community impacted by this loss," the North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services said in a statement obtained by news outlets.
A North Carolina teenager has died from a rare and often fatal infection caused by an amoeba found in warm freshwater, state health officials said. (GoFundMe)
The teen’s death was reported just days after an 8-year-old girl in Louisiana succumbed to the infection.

"While these infections are very rare, this is an important reminder that this amoeba is present in our state and across the U.S.," State Epidemiologist Zack Moore, M.D., said in a prior statement. "There are steps people can take to reduce their risk of infection while swimming during the warmer months."
DOCTORS THOUGHT MAN HAD BRAIN CANCER — THEY FOUND LIVE TAPEWORMS INSTEAD
Naegleria fowleri — commonly referred to as a "brain-eating amoeba" — causes a life-threatening brain infection called primary amebic meningoencephalitis (PAM).
The amoeba is most active in the months that the water temperature stays elevated.

"It's typically this time of year when it's very hot outside, when there hasn't been a lot of rain … and the lakes and ponds get pretty stagnant and get very warm, and that's a great breeding ground for these type of natural inhabitants of those waters," Dr. Jeffrey Kahn, chief of pediatric infectious diseases at UT Southwestern and Children's Health in Dallas, Texas, told Fox News Digital.
A microscopic image shows Naegleria fowleri, the amoeba that causes the rare brain infection primary amoebic meningoencephalitis. (CDC)

The infection can occur when water containing the amoeba is forced up the nose, allowing the amoeba to travel to the brain. This can occur when someone jumps or dives into the water or participates in water sports.
"Once that happens, it's nearly a lethal disease," Kahn warned. "The mortality rate is close to 100%."
Naegleria fowleri does not cause illness via swallowing.
Warning signs to recognize
The initial symptoms of PAM usually begin about five days after exposure, but they can be noticed sooner.
Early signs usually include headache, nausea, fever and/or vomiting, the CDC’s website states.
As the infection progresses, people may experience confusion, slurred speech, stiff neck, disorientation, hallucinations, seizures and coma.
"By the time the [amoeba] enters the brain and starts to basically erode the brain tissue, it's too late."
"The initial symptoms are actually quite nonspecific — they don't point to one disease or another — but they can progress very rapidly," Kahn noted.
Diagnosis involves testing cerebrospinal fluid obtained through a spinal tap; specialized laboratory testing may be needed.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER
Symptoms usually begin about five days after exposure, although they can appear anywhere from one to 12 days later. Once symptoms start, the disease progresses rapidly.
Most people die within one to 18 days after symptoms begin, typically around five days, per the CDC.
Prevention of infection
To prevent potentially fatal infections, Kahn recommends either avoiding the types of waters where the amoeba is likelier to be found, or taking added precautions.
The amoeba is most active in the months that the water temperature stays elevated. (iStock)
"If you are swimming in those waters, wear a nose clip, don't put your head underwater, those types of things," he said.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES
Drinking contaminated water does not present a risk, and the infection does not spread from one person to another.
Because the amoeba is found in soil, the CDC also recommends avoiding stirring up the sediment at the bottom of lakes, ponds and rivers.
Treatment of brain-eating amoebas

When a patient has been diagnosed with a brain-eating amoeba, treatment involves a combination of antimicrobial and anti-amoebic medications, including amphotericin B, azithromycin, rifampin and miltefosine.

"There has been a cocktail of antibiotics and antimicrobials that have been tried over the years — but with a very, very small number of cases every year, it's tough to draw any conclusions from that," Kahn said.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"In the cases we've seen, we typically throw a lot of these antibiotics as a therapeutic modality, but by the time the [amoeba] enters the brain and starts to basically erode the brain tissue, it's too late."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Those who experience sudden headache, fever, stiff neck or vomiting — especially if they have recently been swimming in warm freshwater — should seek immediate medical attention, the CDC recommends.
