title: 80-year-old Dem beats back generational challenge after going all-in on trans athletes
summary: Ed Markey defeated Seth Moulton's generational change campaign by leaning into progressive credentials and taking a bold stance on transgender rights in sports.
story: Incumbent Sen. Ed Markey, D-Mass., and Rep. Seth Moulton, D-Mass., faced off over transgender athletes, ICE, socialism and term limits in their final debate before the Sept. 1 Democratic primary. (Credit: WCVB)
One of the only Democrats stumping for transgender rights on the campaign trail fought back a younger challenger pushing generational change in the Senate.

Sen. Ed Markey, D-Mass., withstood a challenge from Rep. Seth Moulton, D-Mass., to again be crowned as Massachusetts’ Democratic nominee for Senate in his quest for a third full term on Tuesday night. The Associated Press projected Markey would defeat Moulton less than an hour after polls closed.

Markey, who has represented Massachusetts in Congress for nearly five decades, survived Moulton’s campaign focused on generational change by leaning into his progressive bona fides. Notably, he is one of the few Democrats running this midterm cycle who is continuing to push for transgender rights, particularly in sports.
TOP 5 MOST HEATED MOMENTS AS PROGRESSIVES SPAR OVER WHO IS FURTHER TO THE LEFT IN FINAL DEM SENATE DEBATE

Sen. Ed Markey, D-Mass., and Rep. Seth Moulton, D-Mass., are vying for the Democratic nomination in a race defined by demands for generational change. (Andrew Harnik/Getty Images; Michael Brochstein/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images)
"Trans athletes should be able to play," Markey told The New York Times. "That reflects Massachusetts and who we are. And Seth Moulton does not."

The position, which has been used by Republicans as a political rallying cry on the campaign trail and one that Democrats have largely remained quiet about as they push to flip both chambers of Congress, is one that Moulton argued played a major factor in Democrats’ losing across the board in 2024.
"I have two little girls, I don’t want them getting run over on a playing field by a male or formerly male athlete, but as a Democrat I’m supposed to be afraid to say that," Moulton said at the time.
DEMOCRATS STAY QUIET ON NEXT STEPS AFTER SUPREME COURT TRANSGENDER SPORTS RULING

Given Massachusetts’ position as a deep-blue bastion — the Bay State hasn’t had a Republican senator since 2013; former Sen. Scott Brown lost to Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass. — it’s unlikely that Markey’s position will cost him in November.

And his primary victory marks another win for progressives. Markey, who co-authored the Green New Deal resolution years ago, boasted the backing of progressive titans, including Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y.
WATCH: LAWMAKERS REVEAL WHERE THEY STAND ON CONGRESSIONAL TERM LIMITS AFTER RECENT HEALTH SCARES

Sen. Ed Markey and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez attend a press conference to celebrate the 5-year anniversary of the Green New Deal in front of the U.S. Capitol Building in Washington, D.C., on Feb. 6, 2024. (Yasin Ozturk/Anadolu via Getty Images)

It also serves as a blow to a broader push among Democrats across the country looking for generational change, particularly after the tumult that followed former President Joe Biden and his attempt to run for a second term in the White House.

Though longtime incumbents have been defeated, including Rep. John Larson, D-Conn., 78, by the much younger Hartford Mayor Luke Bronin, 47, Markey was able to hold on despite Moulton making age a key factor in his campaign.
For his own part, Moulton, after losing the primary on Tuesday evening, said he viewed his campaign as a necessary challenge to even the party's most tenured figures.

"Challenging the establishment and calling for a new generation of leadership isn’t easy, but it is necessary. I will continue to push the Democratic Party — and our country — to look towards the future," Moulton said in a statement.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Markey’s victory over Moulton isn’t the first time that a younger candidate has stepped into the arena only to be felled by the octogenarian.

Markey bested Massachusetts political royalty in 2020, beating former Rep. Joe Kennedy III in a primary contest that, like his contentious battle against Moulton, centered on a changing of the guard in the upper chamber.
Alex Miller is a writer for Fox News Digital covering the U.S. Senate.

title: Scandal-plagued 'Squad' rep cruises to Democratic nomination with no GOP roadblocks in view
summary: Ayanna Pressley faces no challengers in the Massachusetts 7th district, but controversies over her husband's federal contract and finances loom large.
story: Fox News chief congressional correspondent Chad Pergram reports on Rep. Ayanna Pressley’s finances coming under scrutiny after her net worth swelled to an estimated $8 million on ‘Special Report.’
Rep. Ayanna Pressley, D-Mass., is officially the Democratic nominee for Massachusetts' 7th Congressional District after facing no challengers in Tuesday's primary.

But despite controversies involving Pressley's personal finances, her husband and racially charged remarks she's made, the "Squad member" will face no Republican candidate in the November general election.

Pressley's district encompasses roughly three-quarters of Boston, and the Cook Political Report ranks it as Solid Democrat. She was first elected to office in 2018, alongside Squad members Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., and Rep. Rashida Tlaib, D-Mich.

Although Pressley faced no competition in the primary or general election, she joined other Democratic candidates on the campaign trail, including state Rep. Rep. Ayanna Pressley, D-Mass., speaks during a campaign rally in support of the statewide Massachusetts Democratic ticket, Wednesday, Nov. 2, 2022, in Boston. (AP Photo/Mary Schwalm)

title: DOJ lawsuit targets alleged school ‘secret gender transitions’ policies that keep parents in the dark
summary: The DOJ lawsuit against Kansas City, Kansas Public Schools alleges "secret" gender transition plans locked parents out, violating FERPA and PPRA.
story: Assistant Attorney General for Civil Rights at the Department of Justice Harmeet Dhillon tells Fox News Digital other school district investigations are coming after a first-of-its-kind lawsuit against Kansas City, Kansas Public Schools over alleged ‘secret’ student gender transitions without their parents’ knowledge or consent.

The Department of Justice (DOJ) is investigating other school districts and contemplating additional lawsuits over alleged violations of federal parental rights laws, Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon told Fox News Digital Tuesday, calling the DOJ's newly filed "first-of-its-kind" case against Kansas City, Kansas Public Schools the "first of many."

The DOJ sued Kansas City, Kansas Public Schools (KCKPS) Tuesday, alleging the district violated the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) and the Protection of Pupil Rights Amendment (PPRA) with a district policy that facilitates "secret gender transitions" for students at school without their parents’ knowledge or consent.

"No, we're not waiting. What we do is we ask for documents, we investigate and then we try to resolve cases with school districts. And if we cannot, then we file lawsuits. And, so, there are many other lawsuits contemplated here and other investigations that are ongoing," Dhillon said when asked whether DOJ would wait for the Kansas case to conclude before pursuing other districts.
Dhillon declined to identify the other districts under investigation, saying she did not want to prejudge the outcomes.
EXCLUSIVE: HOUSE COMMITTEE PROBES CHICAGO PUBLIC SCHOOLS OVER HIDING 'GENDER AFFIRMATION' FROM PARENTS
Assistant Attorney General for Civil Rights Harmeet Dhillon speaks during a news conference in Los Angeles. (Allen J. Schaben/Los Angeles Times via Getty Images)
"This is a really important lawsuit for us. And the point I wanted to emphasize is that it's the first of many," she said.
The DOJ lawsuit against KCKPS centers on internal guidance for transgender and gender non-conforming students. The DOJ alleges the district has used versions of the guidance since 2017.

Under the guidance described in the complaint, students can ask that their parents be excluded from school planning meetings and that their transgender or gender non-conforming status not be disclosed to their parents. The resulting written plans can address names, pronouns, school records, restroom and locker room use, sports and other accommodations.
Asked about KCKPS’ assertion that it complies with federal law, Dhillon rejected the district’s position.
FIRST ON FOX: SCHOOL LIED, HID DAUGHTER'S GENDER TRANSITION UNDER DISTRICT POLICY, PARENTS ALLEGE

Department of Education Secretary Linda McMahon and President Donald Trump at a White House event. The administration has said it will pull federal funding from several school districts across the country over transgender policies. (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images, File)

"Well, I think you can get that from the complaint, but they had secret gender transition plans that locked parents out of knowing what was being asked of their children. So, I obviously completely reject that," Dhillon said.
KCKPS disputed DOJ’s allegations Tuesday in a news release.

"Contrary to the allegations in the complaint, the district maintains that it is in full compliance with FERPA and PPRA and is disappointed by the DOJ’s decision to file the lawsuit," the release read.
The district said it would respond through the federal court process and would not comment further while the litigation is pending.
TRUMP ADMINISTRATION THREATENS KANAS SCHOOL DISTRICT FUNDING OVER TRANSGEDNER STUDENT POLICY

The lawsuit centers on internal guidance for transgender and gender non-conforming students. KCKPS disputed DOJ’s allegations Tuesday in a news release, stating that it is disappointed in the administration's decision to file a lawsuit. (Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP Photo, File)
The DOJ argues the written plans constitute education records under FERPA and that excluding parents can prevent them from exercising their rights to inspect and challenge those records.

The government separately alleges the district violates PPRA by allowing students to participate in meetings and evaluations that can reveal sensitive information without prior written parental consent.
The Department of Education opened a FERPA investigation into KCKPS in August 2025.
The federal government advised the district Aug. 12 that its guidance violated FERPA and PPRA, and the complaint states the government ultimately determined KCKPS would not voluntarily comply.
The DOJ alleges the district violates PPRA by allowing students to participate in sensitive meetings and evaluations without prior written parental consent. (Kobus Louw via Getty Images, File)
The DOJ is asking a federal court to declare the district’s practices unlawful and prohibit enforcement of the guidance or similar policies that violate FERPA or PPRA.
Dhillon said the DOJ intends to pursue potential violations elsewhere.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"But I want there to be a very clear message to every school district in the United States. They are on notice that if they violate FERPA and PPRA, the United States Department of Justice stands ready to protect the rights of parents and the rights to pupils to privacy, dignity and parental rights in determining how children are educated in the United States," Dhillon said.
The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Kansas referred questions about the lawsuit to the DOJ’s Office of Public Affairs.
Brittany Miller is a Fox News Digital breaking news writer and former Independent reporter who graduated from Syracuse University in 2023.

title: Former Florida governor hopeful hauled out of county meeting after protesting Israel investments
summary: James Fischback was forcibly removed from a Miami-Dade commissioners meeting after protesting the county's raised investment limit in Israel bonds.
story: James Fischback opposes Miami Dade County’s proposal to increase Israeli investments

James Fischback, a former Florida gubernatorial candidate and controversial political figure, was forcibly removed from a Miami-Dade Board of County Commissioners meeting Tuesday afternoon after protesting the county's expanded investment in Israel-backed bonds.

"Do you serve the people of Hialeah or of Haifa? Do you serve the people of Aventura or of Tel Aviv? Do you serve the people of South Miami or of Jerusalem? This money should be invested here in this community. It should be invested in Miami-Dade County," he added before officers escorted him from the room.

The confrontation comes after the county voted earlier this summer to raise its investment cap with Israel from 3% to 5% of its portfolio — a move that allows it invest upwards of about $400 million to $450 million. The change has drawn opposition from figures like Fischback critical of using public funds to invest in Israel as the war in Gaza continues to fuel political divisions in the U.S. It has also provided Fischback a platform to continue his opposition to U.S.-Israel ties.
ANTISEMITISM FIGHT EXPLODES IN FLORIDA AS VOTERS HEAD TO THE POLLS: 'POLITICAL POGROM'

GOP gubernatorial candidate James Fishback announces Sean Lozano, a South Florida police officer, as his running mate during a press conference on Thursday, June 25, 2026. (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect)
"What this is about, very simply, is whom do you serve?" Fischback said.
Fischback, a Republican, has garnered national attention for his views on race and has developed a reputation for confrontational public appearances.

Fischback was among the 11 GOP candidates seeking to replace outgoing Gov. Ron DeSantis. He garnered 10.4% of the vote in the Aug. 18 primary but drew national attention for a series of inflammatory on-camera moments.
In one such case, he repeatedly called Rep. Byron Donalds, the frontrunner, eventual nominee and one of the only Black Republicans in Congress, a "slave" repeatedly at a news conference.

"Byron Donalds is a slave. I’m sorry, he’s a slave. He is a slave to his donors. He is a slave to the corporate interests, to the tech bros that want to turn our state into, in his own words, a financial capital," Fischback said.
He would later shout a similar phrase at Donalds directly, catching Donalds on the way back to his car with a megaphone and a throng of supporters.
"You’re a DEI hire. You’re a slave. Go back to New York," Fischback yelled.
JOSH SHAPIRO WARNS THAT ATTACKS ON AIPAC ARE BEING USED TO 'SILENCE CERTAIN VOTERS'
Rep. Byron Donalds, who has received backing from President Donald Trump, is running for Florida governor. (Al Diaz/Getty Images)
Fischback's comments on Tuesday weren't the only ones that expressed outrage over the portfolio change.

Other members of the public who expressed concern about the change voiced disappointment that the county would put public investment dollars behind Israel, given the politically charged atmosphere around the topic of its relations with the U.S.
Another woman who identified herself as Ivar Fandel walked to the podium wearing a "let Gaza live" shirt.

"Item 5B does exist in the context of a budget crisis as well as a genocide against Palestinians in Gaza at the hands of Israel," Fandel said, referring to the agenda item discussing the county's change.

During his campaign, Fischback positioned himself as one of the only Republican candidates to decline contributions from the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC). He also pledged to divest from Israel-backed bonds.

"Florida has a specific policy. You’re not allowed to use taxpayer funds to buy foreign government bonds, with one exception: Israel. And so my premise is, first principles, we should not be lending taxpayer pensioner money to any foreign government," Fischback said in an interview with the American Conservative.
He also blasted several candidates, including Donalds, for what he characterized as "singular allegiance" to Israel.
HUCKABEE WARNS OF 'BIBLICAL IGNORANCE' AS HE DEFENDS CONSERVATIVE SUPPORT FOR ISRAEL
James Fishback, a Republican, is a Florida gubernatorial candidate. (Fishback for Florida campaign)
SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

"I think people like Randy Fine and other AIPAC politicians have a singular allegiance. And that allegiance is to the best interests of Israel. The idea of saying ‘I am running to represent a foreign country’s interest in the United States Congress’ is preposterous. They’re buying allegiance," Fischback said in a post to X.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Fischback did not immediately respond to requests for comment from Fox News Digital.
Leo Briceno is a politics reporter for the congressional team at Fox News Digital. He was previously a reporter with World Magazine.

title: Republicans turn on House GOP lawmaker accused of late-night texts, lavish gifts to female staffers
summary: Several House Republicans joined Democrats to censure Chuck Edwards after an ethics probe found he created a hostile work environment for staffers.
story: Trey Gowdy calls out current and former members of Congress facing harassment allegations, demanding clear rules and robust enforcement to protect young staffers on Capitol Hill from misconduct.

Nearly every House Republican joined all Democrats to admonish one of their own after a bombshell investigation found that the lawmaker had engaged in "unprofessional and inappropriate conduct" with his staff.

The House voted to censure Rep. Chuck Edwards, R-N.C., on a landslide 413 to 2 vote as Congress has grappled with multiple incidents of alleged sexual harassment and misconduct by lawmakers on both sides of the aisle. Only Edwards and Rep. Ralph Norman, R-S.C., voted against the resolution.

The censure vote on Tuesday comes on the heels of a bombshell House Ethics Committee report released last month that recommended Edwards be rebuked for "persistent unprofessional and inappropriate conduct towards two young female staffers."
BAD BOSSES ON CAPITOL HILL COULD FACE RECKONING UNDER NEW ANONYMOUS STAFFER REVIEW PLATFORM
Rep. Chuck Edwards, R-N.C., listens during a House Budget Committee markup meeting on Capitol Hill on May 16, 2025, in Washington, D.C. (Getty Images)
The committee is chaired by Edwards' fellow Republican Rep. Michael Guest, R-Miss., but acts on a bipartisan basis to investigate lawmakers on both sides of the aisle.

Guest noted on the House floor that the investigation did not find evidence that Edwards engaged in sexual activity, nor did he explicitly proposition the staffers, but that his "conduct toward two young female staffers was inappropriate and violated rules prohibiting sexual harassment," and that it created a hostile work environment.

"The committee found that Representative Edwards was, at a minimum, blind to the reality and at worst dismissive of the impact his conduct had on the career and well-being of the women on his staff," Guest said.
REPLACEMENT GOP NOMINEE NAMED AFTER REP CHUCK EDWARDS DROPS RE-ELECTION BID

Ahead of the vote, Edwards told Fox News Digital, "They’ll make their argument, and I’ll make mine," and countered that the House Ethics Committee had abandoned "its own rules" in its handling of his case.

That report detailed lavish gifts, trips, and the reading of a poem to one of the staffers, going to a staffer's home to perform chores, late-night personal texts, and taking one of the staffers to a casino, among other interactions. He ended his bid for re-election two days after its release.

He disputed the report on the House floor — after apologizing to the pair of staffers at the center of the Ethics Committee’s probe, along with his wife and family — accusing the bipartisan panel of cherry-picking the context of the incidents to fit a specific narrative.
He challenged the censure vote at hand and contended that his regret over the situation was "not an admission of sexual harassment."

"Generosity is not sexual harassment. Caring deeply about the people with whom you've worked for years is not sexual harassment," Edwards said. "And conduct that is otherwise permissible does not automatically become misconduct, simply because enough individual moments are assembled together and viewed through the darkest possible ends."
CAPITOL SEX SCANDALS SPARK PUSH TO BAN HOUSE LAWMAKERS FROM SLEEPING WITH STAFFERS

Reps. Tony Gonzales, R-Texas, and Eric Swalwell, D-Calif., are expected to face expulsion votes this week over sexual misconduct allegations if they do not resign. (Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc.; Win McNamee/Getty Images)
Still, his arguments weren’t enough to dissuade his colleagues. Notably, the entirety of House Republican leadership voted for the resolution.

Rep. Teresa Leger Fernández, D-N.M., who chairs the Democratic Women’s Caucus, contended that since Edwards "continues to show no remorse, it's obvious that Edwards refuses to understand sexual harassment or his abuse of power."
"If we don't take action today, there is no opportunity for these women to receive justice," Leger Fernández said.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Edwards became the 30th member of the House of Representatives to be censured, which carries the penalty of a public rebuke for his conduct but does not force him to resign from his seat.

It also comes as other members of the House have grappled with their colleagues’ conduct in recent months. Earlier this year, former Reps. Eric Swalwell and Tony Gonzales both resigned on the same day.

Swalwell resigned after being hit with allegations of rape and sexual assault, while Gonzales exited Congress after being accused of sexual misconduct with a former staffer, and after he admitted to having an affair with his former staffer, Regina Santos-Aviles, who later died by setting herself on fire.
Both faced the rare threat of expulsion.
Alex Miller is a writer for Fox News Digital covering the U.S. Senate.

title: Spanberger fact-checked after Trump mail-voting warning raises military ballot fears
summary: CNN issued a correction after Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger and Wolf Blitzer suggested Trump's mail-voting rules could impact military voters abroad.
story: Fox News legal editor Kerri Urbahn joins 'Fox & Friends' to analyze lawsuits filed by 24 states and Washington, D.C. against the United States Postal Service regarding mail-in voting rules. Urbahn breaks down the Supreme Court decision and details agency rules requiring barcodes on mail-in ballots.

Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger claimed the Trump administration was attempting to take away the ability of Americans serving overseas to vote by mail — despite the Postal Service’s final rule explicitly exempting military and overseas ballots from its new requirements.

The Postal Service’s (USPS) final rule at the center of the dispute expressly exempts ballots covered by the Uniformed and Overseas Citizens Absentee Voting Act (UOCAVA) from the new federal ballot-mail requirements — though an Obama-appointed federal judge temporarily stayed key provisions of the rule Thursday.

"If you are serving our country abroad, I believe that you should have the ability to cast a vote in our elections. The Trump Administration is attempting to take that ability away," Spanberger wrote on X on Aug. 29.
FEDERAL JUDGE BLOCKS TRUMP ADMINISTRATION FROM RESTRICTING MAIL-IN BALLOTS AHEAD OF MIDTERMS
CNN's Wolf Blitzer, left; Gov. Abigail Spanberger, right. (Annabelle Gordon/Reuters; Kristina Bumphrey/Getty Images)
The final rule says UOCAVA voters are excluded and explains that the separate treatment reflects the circumstances facing military personnel, their families and other overseas voters.

Spanberger made a similar argument during a CNN interview after anchor Wolf Blitzer raised the possibility that Virginia military personnel overseas could be affected. CNN subsequently returned on air to clarify that UOCAVA ballots are exempt from the new USPS requirements.

"The continued attacks that we're seeing from the Trump administration [are] really just an effort to get people fearful, to get to stay home, and in many cases, to eliminate what is a valid, safe, secure way for people to be able to make their voices heard and to vote," she said.
Blitzer added that Virginia is home to "a lot of military personnel who totally rely on mail-in ballots if they want to be able to express their opinion."

Spanberger agreed, pointing to members of the military and diplomatic services, saying the administration’s actions were impacting them along with other Virginians who find vote-by-mail "a better option."
TRUMP SCORES SUPREME COURT WIN ON MAIL-IN VOTING RESTRICTIONS BEFORE MIDTERMS
Spanberger did not respond to a request for comment, but when reached, a representative for CNN said Blitzer issued an on-air correction Monday.

"On Friday, I interviewed the Democratic governor of Virginia, Abigail Spanberger. We discussed legal challenges to the Trump administration's directives for the Postal Service on mail-in voting," Blitzer said in the correction.

"A comment that may’ve suggested that U.S. military and overseas voters' ballots would be impacted by these directives -- I want to be clear right now, those ballots are exempt from the Postal Service's new rules implementing the president's March executive order. Those groups are covered under [UOCAVA], just to be specific on that point."
An X community note added as an appendix to Spanberger's tweet of her exchange with Blitzer also surfaced the correction.

"Military and overseas voters' UOCAVA ballots are explicitly exempt from the USPS rules implementing the March 2026 executive order; service members abroad can still register/request absentee ballots via the Federal Post Card Application," it read.
Several users also pushed back and cited federal statute as well as the USPS’ own rule.
Others said the governor was allegedly "lying" and suggested she should know of UOCAVA as a former CIA officer.

Sen. Mike Lee, R-Utah, picked up on her original tweet, responding that he had personally discussed overseas military voting with Trump "many times" and said Trump had consistently made clear he did not want to interfere with Americans serving abroad voting by mail.
"This is completely false," Lee tweeted.
2028 DEM HOPEFUL SLAPS TRUMP ADMINISTRATION WITH LAWSUIT OVER MAIL-IN VOTING AFTER MAJOR SCOTUS VICTORY
Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger responds to President Donald Trump's, unseen, State of the Union. (Steve Helber/Reuters)
The Supreme Court in August handed Trump a largely favorable procedural ruling, staying an earlier injunction after finding that the states’ challenge was premature at that stage.

The ruling did not decide the legality of the administration’s mail-voting policies on the merits. America First Legal President Gene Hamilton previously told Fox News Digital that the court prevented the administration from being effectively "enjoined from thinking" before agencies had settled on concrete policies.
SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER
The broader fight over Trump’s mail-voting push remains unresolved.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The Supreme Court stayed a judge's earlier injunction after concluding the administration was likely to prevail on its argument that the challenge was premature, but her latest temporary restraining order sets up yet another speed bump.
Born and raised in Allentown, Pennsylvania, worked in both the New York and Washington bureaus for Fox News since 2013.

title: Allies of disgraced ex-House Dem poised for criminal charges for refusing Congress' probe
summary: Allies of a former House Democrat face DOJ criminal charges after the House unanimously held them in contempt of Congress over defied subpoenas.
story: 'America Reports' co-anchor Sandra Smith reports on Rep. Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick stepping down before a formal disciplinary hearing by the House as part of an ethics investigation.
Allies of a former House Democrat under federal indictment are now facing potential criminal charges themselves.

The House of Representatives unanimously agreed to hold two people in contempt of Congress on Tuesday — North Miami Beach, Florida, Mayor Michael Joseph and Hector Roos, a former aide to ex-Rep. Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick, D-Fla. — for failing to work with the House Ethics Committee's investigation into the disgraced Sunshine State Democrat.
It's now up to the Department of Justice (DOJ) whether it pursues criminal charges against both. A contempt of Congress conviction carries a fine of up to $100,000 and up to a year in jail.
DISGRACED DEM CUT OFF FROM DOING BUSINESS WITH GOVERNMENT AFTER ALLEGED ‘OUTRIGHT FRAUD’ UNCOVERED

Then-Rep. Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick takes the oath of office during a ceremonial swearing-in ceremony at Broward County Governmental Center in Fort Lauderdale, Fla., on Jan. 18, 2022. (Carline Jean/South Florida Sun Sentinel/Tribune News Service via Getty Images)

"The committee cannot fulfill its obligations to safeguard the integrity of the House for witnesses, ignore its subpoenas, and the House cannot accept such willful disregard of its authorities. Mr. Roos and Mr. Joseph willfully fail to comply with multiple subpoenas issued by the committee," Committee Chairman Michael Guest, R-Miss., said.

"They impeded the investigative subcommittee's investigations into the allegations concerning former Representative Cherfilus-McCormick. Those allegations were serious and included violations of federal law to which Mr. Roos and Mr. Joseph were party there. Their conduct warrants referrals to the United States Department of Justice for contempt of Congress."
MIKE JOHNSON SAYS HE SUPPORTS EXPELLING SHEILA CHERFILUS-MCCORMICK OVER DOZENS OF ETHICS VIOLATIONS

The measure passed by voice vote on Tuesday afternoon, meaning lawmakers were not individually put on the record over where they stand. Any lawmaker can stand and object to a voice vote and call for a roll call instead, which none did.
The Democrats present instead signaled they were fully in support of the bid against their fellow left-wingers.
FLORIDA DEM FILED FOR RE-ELECTION DAYS BEFORE RESIGNATION AS HOUSE ETHICS COMMITTEE RAMPED UP PRESSURE
Rep. Michael Guest, R-Miss., walks through the Capitol. (Andrew Harnik/Getty Images)

"At a time when public confidence in Congress is at historic lows and the House's ability to self-police member conduct is under intense scrutiny, enforcing lawful congressional process is vital to delivering swift transparency and accountability for any misconduct," Rep. Mark DeSaulnier, D-Calif., said. "A witness who refuses to cooperate with the Ethics Committee hinders the thoroughness and swiftness of an investigation."

Guest charged that Roos "filed inaccurate reports" with the Federal Election Commission while working for Cherfilus-McCormick. He said Roos did not provide adequate justification for not complying with the committee.

"Mr. Joseph was the president of a company that improperly provided corporate funds for the congresswoman's campaign, influenced her staff to submit community funding project requests for entities that he supported," Guest said of the other target.
He said Joseph cited attorney-client privilege in his decision not to comply with the committee, but that lawmakers argued it was not a valid justification to dodge the probe.
INDICTED DEMOCRAT SHEILA CHERFILUS-MCCORMICK REFUSES TO RESIGN AS EXPULSION VOTE LOOMS

Cherfilus-McCormick resigned from Congress earlier this year amid intense pressure from both the left and right. Rep. Greg Steube, R-Fla., had been threatening to push a resolution to expel her at the time.

Rep. Greg Steube, R-Fla., makes his way to a House Republican Conference meeting with President Donald Trump on the budget reconciliation bill in the U.S. Capitol on May 20, 2025. (Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc. via Getty Images)
The DOJ said she and her co-defendants "conspired to steal" $5 million in emergency federal funds and used the money to bankroll her 2021 congressional campaign.
EXCLUSIVE: WOMAN WHO STOLE $1.7M MEANT FOR HURRICANE VICTIMS GETS PRISON TIME AS DHS CRACKS DOWN ON FEMA FRAUD

"According to the indictment, Cherfilus-McCormick, 46, and her brother Edwin Cherfilus, 51, both of Miramar, worked through their family healthcare company on a FEMA-funded COVID-19 vaccination staffing contract in 2021. In July 2021, the company received an overpayment of $5 million in FEMA funds," the DOJ said in November 2025. "Prosecutors allege that a substantial portion of the misappropriated funds was used as candidate contributions to Cherfilus-McCormick’s 2021 congressional campaign and for the personal benefit of the defendants."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
She has pleaded not guilty.

title: Illegal immigrant’s ‘over-the-top’ sexual assault on elderly woman sends sheriff into rage: ‘Out of control’
summary: Sheriff Grady Judd says a 24-year-old illegal immigrant broke into a Polk County home and committed a vicious sexual battery on a 77-year-old woman.
story: Polk County, Florida, Sheriff Grady Judd details the alleged sexual assault by illegal immigrant Axel Antonio Espinal Herrera on an elderly woman. (Credit: X/@PolkCoSheriff, Aug. 31)

A sheriff in the Florida suburbs took to X to voice his outrage over a 24-year-old illegal immigrant allegedly breaking into a local home to conduct an "over-the-top," "vicious sexual battery" on a 77-year-old woman.

Polk County, Florida, Sheriff Grady Judd blasted Honduran illegal immigrant Axel Antonio Espinal Herrera, who he said is was arrested on charges of committing "one of the most horrific crimes that we’ve seen in this county in a very long time."

Though the sheriff voiced his frustration that "this couldn’t have occurred if [Herrera] was not in this country," he promised that his office’s goal is to make sure that Herrera "will be in a United States prison for the rest of his life upon conviction."

"Sexual battery of an individual is without a doubt one of the most horrific crimes that occurs. And a violent, out-of-control sexual battery on a stranger even elevates that one more level. And then you take on top of that the suspect is in this country illegally, that pushes it over the top," said Judd.
EXCLUSIVE: DHS ASKS FLORIDA NOT TO RELEASE ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT ACCUSED OF DRUGGING, RAPING WOMAN AFTER CLUBBING

24-year-old Honduran illegal immigrant Axel Antonio Espinal Herrera (right) was arrested by the Polk County, Florida, Sheriff's Office and is facing charges in connection with a violent sexual assault on a 77-year-old woman. (Courtesy of Polk County, Florida, Sheriff's Office via X)

According to the sheriff’s office, the sexual assault occurred around 4 a.m. on Saturday. A statement by the office said the elderly victim awoke after a noise and saw an unknown man who entered her bedroom, forcibly removed her clothes and sexually battered her, slapping her when she attempted to get away.
The office said the victim "attempted to escape through the front door when the suspect went into the bathroom, but the suspect chased after her and dragged her back inside and choked her."

After the assault, the suspect vacated the scene, which is when the victim contacted the sheriff’s office. Sheriff’s Office detectives canvassed the neighborhood and encountered Herrera in a nearby home with two other illegal immigrants also from Honduras.
WHITE HOUSE BRINGS RECEIPTS AFTER MEDIA CLAIMS NONCRIMINAL ICE ARRESTS ‘SOARING’: ‘FALSE NARRATIVES’
Polk County, Florida, Sheriff Grady Judd voiced outrage at an "out-of-control" sexual assault allegedly carried out by an illegal immigrant. (Polk County, Florida, Sheriff's Office via website)

Herrera was in the shower when detectives first arrived at the house. The office said that Herrera matched the victim’s description and that clothing described by the victim was found in the home. During the detectives’ search, they found multiple scratches on Herrera’s body consistent with the victim’s statements. He was also found to be in possession of cocaine.

Herrera was arrested and taken to the sheriff’s processing center. He is being charged with kidnapping, sexual battery by force, burglary and battery, tampering with evidence, possession of cocaine, possession of drug paraphernalia, loitering and prowling. The sheriff’s office also noted that under Florida law, each charge against Herrera is elevated by one category due to his illegal status, meaning he is facing the possibility of multiple life sentences.

The office said it notified U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), which placed a detainer on Herrera. The two other illegal immigrants found in the house were also taken into custody on ICE holds.
DOZENS OF ILLEGAL ALIEN TRUCK DRIVERS BUSTED WITH LICENSES FROM DEEP BLUE STATES

Polk County Sheriff Grady Judd (left) beside Brevard County Sheriff Wayne Ivey (center) and Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis (right) at the Polk County Sheriff's Office, on April 19, 2021. (Ricardo Ramirez Buxeda/Orlando Sentinel/Tribune News Service via Getty Images)
Judd did not hold back in his disgust for Herrera’s alleged crimes, calling him a "very violent, very dangerous rapist" and his actions "graphically very vile and out of control."

"He was a young man, 24 years of age, sexually battering a 77-year-old woman after he broke into her house in the middle of the night. Do I need to say more?" said the sheriff.
Peter Pinedo is a politics writer for Fox News Digital.

title: Another ActBlue leader pleads Fifth as House investigates alleged foreign donations
summary: ActBlue board member Kimberly Peeler-Allen invoked her Fifth Amendment right during a House probe into alleged foreign donations to the platform.
story: ActBlue board member Kimberly Peeler Allen remains silent while Fox News' Mark Meredith attempts to ask her questions about allegations of foreign influence on the fundraising platform.

Kimberly Peeler-Allen, a board member of the ActBlue Democratic fundraising organization, invoked her Fifth Amendment right not to incriminate herself while testifying during a House probe into alleged foreign donations to ActBlue, sources familiar with the testimony told Fox News.

Allen's appearance on Capitol Hill came amidst a joint probe by the House Administration, Judiciary and Oversight Committees into allegations that ActBlue accepted illicit foreign donations and failed to prevent fraud.
Allen's decision to plead the Fifth follows suit with ActBlue co-founder Matt DeBergalis, who pleaded the Fifth during his closed-door deposition in front of the same three committees on Aug. 20.
FAR-LEFT POLITICIANS STILL USING ACTBLUE AS 88-YEAR-OLD DISPUTES DONATING NEARLY $150,000 TO FUNDRAISING GIANT

The Committee on House Administration first opened a probe into ActBlue in 2023. Chairman Bryan Steil, R-Wis., claimed the group could be potentially accepting foreign or fraudulent donations by neglecting to require a credit card CVV number for contributions.

Kimberly Peeler-Allen, pictured second from the left, attending the 35th Annual Celebrating Women® Breakfast at New York Marriott Marquis Hotel on May 11, 2022, in New York City. Peeler-Allen pleaded the Fifth Amendment on Sept. 1, 2026, during a probe into Democratic fundraising platform ActBlue, for which she is a member of the board of directors. (Monica Schipper/Getty Images for The New York Women's Foundation)
Steil, in a Tuesday interview with Fox News' Mark Meredith, expressed consternation over the ActBlue-affiliated individuals' refusal to cooperate with the investigation.
ACTBLUE SCRUTINY FUELS NEW GOP BILLS TO TIGHTEN ELECTION DONATION RULES
"I've been frustrated, that individuals [in] ActBlue haven't answered our questions on the record," he told Meredith.

"We've had individuals come, in public testimony, and plead the Fifth. They have a right to do that. And I understand why they did that. But I think the American people deserve to know exactly what's going on. We have an entity here with ActBlue, that has raised roughly $20 billion since its creation. And moved that into Democratic campaigns and Democratic causes. We want to make sure that they have the fraud preventions. We want to make sure that they have the fraud prevention protocols in place to make sure that foreign funds are not coming into U.S. elections," he said.

Chairman Bryan Steil, R-Wis., arrives for the House Administration Committee hearing titled "Preventing Fraudulent Donations: Transparency, Verification, and Accountability," in Longworth building on Wednesday, June 10, 2026. The witness, Regina Wallace-Jones, CEO of ActBlue, invoked her Fifth Amendment privilege. (Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images)
HOUSE DEM LASHES OUT AT GOP EFFORTS TO PROBE FOREIGN DONATIONS WITH STUNNING CLAIM ON MOTIVE
Responding to allegations that the investigation into ActBlue is partisan in nature, Steil rebuked the notion.

"This investigation began is a review of online fundraising platforms and a determination whether or not those platforms had fraud prevention programs in place to prevent foreign funds from coming into U.S. elections. One of those, ActBlue, has been called out by The New York Times [for] having misled or lied to Congress. We're trying to get to the bottom of that exactly what has been taking place inside Act Blue, per the public reporting," he told Meredith.
KEY HOUSE COMMITTEE SCHEDULES HEARING WITH EMBATTLED ACTBLUE CEO: 'NEEDS TO COME CLEAN'

In an April investigative report, The New York Times revealed that ActBlue's legal counsel advised the organization that, in a letter to House Republicans, ActBlue's chief executive Regina Wallace-Jones may have misled lawmakers.
Responding to a congressional inquiry, Wallace-Jones characterized the organization's screening process to ensure its donations were not foreign as "multilayered," according to the report.

title: House Dems overwhelmingly reject anti-socialism resolution after 2 moderates defy Jeffries
summary: House Democrats were split on a vote to condemn socialism after two Democrats helped Republicans push their agenda forward.
story: House GOP Conference Chairwoman Lisa McClain spoke with Fox News Digital about the fight against socialists and a pair of votes in Congress to test House Democrats' resolve.
The House of Representatives passed a resolution condemning socialism on Tuesday evening, with all but eight House Democrats voting against it.

In a stunning twist of fate, however, the vote would not have occurred if two House Democrats hadn't stepped in hours earlier to help the GOP through a procedural hurdle — blindsiding House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., in the process.
Jeffries later threatened consequences for the pair in a dramatic statement late on Tuesday night, calling their move a "breach of trust."

The resolution passed 220 to 192 with all "no" votes coming from the left, including Democrats’ senior leaders: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., House Minority Whip Katherine Clark, D-Mass., and House Democratic Caucus Chair Pete Aguilar, D-Calif.
JOHNSON SCORES WIN AS CONSERVATIVE REBELS END HOUSE FLOOR BLOCKADE OVER VOTER ID BILL
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries speaks during a news conference at the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C., US, on Friday, Oct. 3, 2025. (Graeme Sloan/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
The legislation also affirmed support for election integrity and called for passage of the Safeguarding American Voter Eligibility (SAVE) Act, which nearly all Democrats oppose.

House conservatives had threatened to tank a procedural vote, called a "rule vote," meant to unlock debate on several bills GOP leaders wanted lawmakers to vote on this week. That included the resolution condemning socialism and several other unrelated bills.

Five Republicans voted against the rule, which was poised to fail until Reps. Jared Golden, D-Maine, and Marie Gluesenkamp Perez, D-Wash., provided two critical votes to get the GOP over the finish line in a narrow 209 to 208 vote.

Jeffries and other senior House Democratic leaders warned in a statement the day after, ""The decision by two of our colleagues to blindside the entire House Democratic Caucus and join with the Republican majority to pass a procedural rule on the brink of failing represents a significant breach of trust."
"It is an action that necessitates a serious response, and we have asked the Committee on Caucus Rules to take this up in short order," the leaders said.
All Republicans wound up voting in favor of the resolution condemning socialism and affirming election integrity on Tuesday evening, however.
TENSIONS ERUPT IN HOUSE HEARING AS GOP ADVANCES ANTI-SOCIALISM RESOLUTION WHILE DEMS RAGE: 'SILLY SEASON'

Golden and Gluesenkamp Perez were among the Democrats who joined the GOP in that vote, as well as Reps. Don Davis, D-N.C., Vicente Gonzalez, D-Texas, Henry Cuellar, D-Texas, Kathy Castor, D-Fla., Gabe Vasquez, D-N.M., and Darren Soto, D-Fla. Reps. Maggie Goodlander, D-N.H., and Chrissy Houlahan, D-Pa., voted "present."

Socialism has dominated the 2026 midterm election season on both sides of the aisle. Democrats are grappling with a far-left insurgency within their ranks as candidates linked to the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) continue to topple incumbents and establishment-backed candidates across the country.
It's provided fodder for the House GOP while it fights an uphill battle to keep control of Congress in November as Republicans warn the socialist left will take over the Democratic Party if it wins.

Speaker of the House Mike Johnson, R-La., talks to reporters outside his office on day 28 of the government shutdown, at the Capitol in Washington, Tuesday, Oct. 28, 2025.  (J. Scott Applewhite/AP Photo)

"Socialism has failed everywhere it's been tried without exception. It's a dangerous ideology that creates misery for the very people it claims to help," Republican Study Committee Chairman August Pfluger, R-Texas, told Fox News Digital. "Today's vote puts the Left on the record and removes any doubt about where my colleagues on the other side of the aisle stand."

Rep. Jeff Crank, R-Colo., who led the resolution, told Fox News Digital, "The resolution is pretty easy, right? It condemns socialism in all its forms, including the DSA, recommits ourselves to the Constitution of the United States…a third point is that we don't want non-citizens voting in elections."
"They can certainly be critical, but it's just a quick choice for the American people to see where people stand on this stuff," Crank said.

But Democrats contended that Republicans' largely symbolic resolution was a meaningless political exercise that does nothing to help Americans with their everyday problems. Many on the left have also dismissed the GOP's election integrity efforts as voter suppression.

"So you're concerned about rising gas, or are you concerned about grocery prices? You know, don't worry. Republicans in Congress are passing another non-binding resolution condemning socialism," Rep. Jim McGovern, D-Mass., said during a hearing on Monday.

The Tuesday evening vote would not have been possible without Golden and Gluesenkamp Perez rescuing Republicans' agenda. Golden is not running for re-election, while Gluesenkamp Perez is one of the most vulnerable Democrats in the country.
It's almost unheard of for the minority party to help their political rivals pass a rule, and Jeffries told reporters he was not notified beforehand.
The five House Republicans who voted against it were Reps. Pete Sessions, R-Texas; Chip Roy, R-Texas; Ralph Norman, R-S.C., Clay Higgins, R-La.; and Andy Harris, R-Md.
Rep. Jared Golden, D-Maine, attends a news conference in the Capitol Visitor Center in Washington, July 17, 2025. (Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The rebels' issue was not with the measure itself, nor the bills it would have allowed the House to pass. Their votes were a protest against how their leaders handled a plan to avert a government shutdown just before the midterm elections, a short-term funding bill called a continuing resolution (CR). That measure passed just before the rule vote began.

But the five GOP lawmakers took issue with how the Senate modified an original House-passed CR, including adding an unrelated measure to delay a congressionally approved hemp product ban by 30 days and a provision curbing the Trump administration’s control over federal grants.

It's worth noting that Golden is also co-lead of a bill aimed at pausing new federal restrictions on certain American lobster and crab fishing industries, which would have also been stalled if the rule failed.
Elizabeth Elkind is a politics reporter for Fox News Digital leading coverage of the House of Representatives. Previous digital bylines seen at Daily Mail and CBS News.

title: Baby killed after illegal immigrant allegedly strikes family at grocery store parking lot
summary: A nine-month-old died after Maria Cobon-Guzman allegedly struck a family in a New Jersey parking lot, reigniting debate over the state's sanctuary policy.
story: ICE arrested Giovana Mercedes Moreno Ochompy, a former Illinois high school teacher and illegal immigrant, in connection with a triple murder involving the Venezuelan Tren de Aragua gang. Chicago police initially released her due to sanctuary city policies, without notifying ICE. Tom Homan, former acting ICE director, criticizes these policies, arguing they hinder federal law enforcement and endanger public safety.

An illegal immigrant from Guatemala was charged with manslaughter after allegedly crashing into a mother and her two children, killing her 9-month-old son, in a New Jersey grocery store parking lot Friday, according to authorities.

A 9-month-old boy was pronounced dead at Jersey Shore University Medical Center in Neptune after Maria Cobon-Guzman allegedly struck his mother and the baby carriage carrying him and his 5-year-old sister in the parking lot of a kosher grocery store in Jackson on Friday.

"An innocent baby would still be alive today had it not been for Joe Biden’s disastrous open border and reckless immigration policy that released countless illegal aliens into our country," a DHS spokesperson told Fox News Digital.
EXCLUSIVE: DHS ANNOUNCES NEW JERSEY ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT ARRESTS AS NEWARK PROTESTS RAGE OUTSIDE FACILITY
Gov. Mikie Sherrill, left; Maria Cobon-Guzman, inset (Jim Watson/Getty Images; Ocean County Sheriff's Office)

"We are urging the Ocean County Jail to honor ICE’s detainers on these two criminal illegal aliens to take them out of American communities once and for all," the spokesperson said of the Republican-friendly county in the otherwise blue state.

Another woman, Ariadna Lazaro-Flores, was also charged in the incident after she reportedly allowed Cobon-Guzman to drive her car knowing she was unlicensed. An inmate report listed Lazaro-Flores as charged with "endangering the welfare of an incompetent person."
Both women illegally entered the U.S. during the Biden administration, with Lazaro-Flores doing so five times in October 2023 and being removed each time, DHS told Fox News Digital.
"She last illegally entered the United States through the Biden Administration’s open border at an unknown place and time," the agency said.
ICE MAKES NATIONWIDE ARRESTS OF ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS, MURDERERS, PEDOPHILES IN HOLIDAY BLITZ
Cobon-Guzman entered once but was released unvetted into the nation’s interior, DHS added. On July 31, an immigration judge issued an order of removal against her.
"New Jersey must honor ICE's detainers on these two criminal illegal aliens to take them out of American communities once and for all,"," the agency tweeted.
Democratic New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill, who signed legislation codifying New Jersey’s Immigrant Trust Directive, had not commented as of Tuesday morning.
When reached for comment, a Sherrill spokesman directed Fox News Digital to Attorney General Jennifer Davenport. Davenport did not immediately respond.
Observers took notice of the relative silence as Sherrill's social media posts about other things including a critique of President Donald Trump's battle with Iran sparked outrage:
"How about sticking to doing something about the highest property taxes in the US [or] stopping illegals from killing and maiming us?" read one response.

"Despite being deported from the United States five times and being previously charged with operating a motor vehicle without a license, Ariadna Lazaro-Flores—the owner of the vehicle that caused the death of a nine-month-old baby and the hospitalizations of his mother and five-year-old sister—was still able to obtain a driver’s license in New Jersey. That is shocking," Smith said.

He added that the tragedy was "completely avoidable, if not for the Biden Administration’s lax and grossly irresponsible immigration enforcement policies. Criminals who are in this country illegally should not be and should never have been able to obtain a driver’s license, either personal or commercial, in the United States."
The Trust Directive, as drafted by Davenport predecessor Gurbir Grewal, limits voluntary assistance New Jersey law enforcement may provide DHS.
New Jersey Republicans fired back at Trenton leadership, suggesting they created the conditions to allow the tragedy to occur.

title: DHS secretary bashes New York leadership after announcing thousands of arrests in sweeping operation
summary: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin says Operation Rotten Apple arrested over 2,100 criminals in New York while blasting the state's sanctuary policies.
story: Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin defended strict immigration enforcement and details plans to hunt down and deport those in the country illegally. He also criticized New York leaders for failing to cooperate on law and order.

Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin detailed the arrest of thousands of individuals in New York considered to be public safety threats during a press conference Tuesday announcing the success of the federal Operation Rotten Apple.

During the announcement, Mullin blasted New York's leadership, including Democratic Gov. Kathy Hochul and New York City's democratic socialist Mayor Zohran Mamdani, for working against law enforcement.

"Operation Rotten Apple was initiated because New York City has a liberal, socialist mayor who, instead of working with law enforcement, tried to cut NYPD's budget by $22 million and refused to cooperate with federal law enforcement. You also have a governor who refuses to work with us. Over the last 30 days, Operation Rotten Apple has taken over 2,100 of the worst criminals off our streets statewide," Mullin said.
ICE MAKES NATIONWIDE ARRESTS OF ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS, MURDERERS, PEDOPHILES IN HOLIDAY BLITZ
Mullin specifically cited the cases of three foreign nationals, each with violent criminal histories.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin speaks during a news conference at the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services New York field office on Sept. 1, 2026, in New York City, N.Y. (Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images)
One arrestee was a 39year-old Indian national with an International Criminal Police Organization (INTERPOL) red notice out on him for an alleged rape he was charged with in Germany, Mullin relayed.
ICE ARRESTS ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS CONVICTED OF ATTEMPTED MURDER, RAPE AND CHILD SEX CRIMES IN TARGETED CRACKDOWN
Another, a 50-year-old Ukrainian citizen, has a lengthy criminal history that includes convictions for kidnapping, abduction, possession of a weapon and murder, Mullin said.
Mullin said the individuals were roaming New York's streets because of the city and state's sanctuary policies.
DHS DEMANDS NEW YORK SANCTUARY POLITICIANS HONOR DETAINER FOR MAN CONVICTED OF RAPING CORPSE ON SUBWAY

"These individuals should never have been on our streets. While radical-left sanctuary states protect illegal immigrants, the Trump administration and ICE (Immigration and Customs Enforcement) officers are out there every day protecting Americans," he said.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin speaks during a news conference at the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services New York field office on Sept. 1, 2026, in New York City. (Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images)

He also claimed New York's Democratic politicians have successfully lobbied for the release of over 13,000 illegal immigrants, while imploring those politicians to cease obstructing DHS and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents from doing their jobs.
MAMDANI SAYS EVEN IF HE CAN GET ALONG WITH TRUMP, HE STILL DEMANDS THAT 'ICE SHOULD BE ABOLISHED'

"Earlier this summer, the mayor of New York City said he believes ICE raids are 'cruel, inhumane and do nothing to protect public safety.' Are you telling me that taking these arrested individuals off the street is not in the interest of public safety? We took them off the streets to protect New Yorkers, while the mayor refuses to cooperate and attempts to slash NYPD's budget. He is extremely out of touch with what the American people want and what public safety looks like," Mullin added.
Mullin specifically bashed Hochul for terminating 287(g) agreements, which allow local municipalities' police departments to coordinate and work with federal agents.
"Keep in mind that seven of the safest cities in the country cooperate with ICE and the 287(g) program," he said.
HOCHUL REMAINS DEFIANT AFTER SHERIFFS SUE OVER LAW BANNING COOPERATION WITH ICE: 'BRING IT ON'

"In private, almost every sheriff and police chief wants to work with us. They took an oath to enforce the law, but radical local politicians prevent them from doing their jobs. I thank the sheriffs who stand up against local political interference on behalf of their constituents. Restoring law and order is an issue supported by 80% of the public across party lines," Mullin continued.

He also revealed that the federal government is willing and able to send more federal agents into New York and other cities where leadership refuses to cooperate with federal law and immigration enforcement.
BORDER CZAR HOMAN VOWS TO 'FLOOD' NEW YORK WITH ICE AGENTS DESPITE HOCHUL'S RESISTANCE

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin speaks during a news conference at the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services New York field office on Sept. 1, 2026, in New York City. (Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images)

title: Dad of girl left permanently disabled in crash with illegal immigrant rips Dems: ‘I reject your sympathy’
summary: Marcus Coleman rejected Democratic lawmakers' sympathy at a Capitol Hill hearing, saying his daughter's permanent injuries are the "end result" of sanctuary cities.
story: The father of a 7-year-old girl left permanently disabled after an illegal immigrant driving an 18-wheeler slammed into the vehicle she was traveling in tore into Democratic lawmakers during a Capitol Hill hearing Tuesday, rejecting their expressions of sympathy and accusing them of failing families like his.

The father of a 7-year-old girl left permanently disabled after an illegal immigrant driving an 18-wheeler slammed into the vehicle she was traveling in tore into Democratic lawmakers during a fiery Capitol Hill hearing Tuesday, rejecting their expressions of sympathy and accusing them of failing families like his.

"I reject your guys’ sympathy," Marcus Coleman, whose daughter Dalilah suffered a fractured skull, broken femur and traumatic brain injury in the 2024 California crash, told lawmakers during a House Judiciary Subcommittee on Immigration Integrity, Security, and Enforcement hearing on sanctuary policies across the United States.
Coleman said Democratic lawmakers had "never reached out to me" after his daughter’s catastrophic injuries.
GRIEVING MOTHERS SCORCH DEM LAWMAKER AFTER HE PIVOTS DURING HEARING TO ATTACK 'MAGA REPUBLICANS'

Marcus Coleman holds his daughter Dalilah Coleman as President Donald Trump delivers his State of the Union address during a joint session of Congress Feb. 24. Coleman criticized Rep. Steve Cohen, D-Tenn., and other lawmakers who oppose efforts to arrest and deport illegal immigrants. (Win McNamee/Getty Images)

"Not one of you guys have ever sat there and seen me in the hallways and said, ‘Hey, sorry about your daughter.’ You guys do it right here where you guys are grandstanding on top of your soapbox," Coleman said. "This is when you guys care. Right here inside this room is the only time you guys care."
Coleman said his daughter "doesn’t deserve" what happened to her.
Dalilah Coleman was seriously injured in a crash allegedly caused by an illegal immigrant. (DHS)

"She didn't ask for any of this," the father said. "The people that jumped the fence did though. They knew exactly what they were doing. They still chose to move forward in that direction. And every day something's happening to somebody, and it is your guys' fault. I hold each and every one of you responsible for it, and I always will."
Dalilah was critically injured in Southern California in 2024 when an 18-wheel tractor-trailer traveling at 60 mph slammed into a vehicle she was riding in.

Authorities identified the truck driver as Partap Singh, an illegal immigrant from India who had obtained a commercial driver's license in California. Singh was driving at an unsafe speed and failed to stop for traffic in a construction zone before the crash, authorities said.

"I'm no longer truck driving. I no longer make the money that we used to make. I'm now pinching pennies," Coleman said. "I have nine kids, by the way, that I take care of, and I had to sit there and stretch that."
ANGEL FAMILIES PLEAD WITH LEADERS TO 'CHOOSE' AMERICAN CHILDREN OVER PROTECTING ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS
Another parent testifying at Tuesday’s hearing described the lasting toll a separate crash involving an illegal immigrant has taken on her family.
Patricia Fox said her daughter, Carissa "Luu" Aspnes, was permanently disabled after a March 2025 hit-and-run crash in Colorado involving an illegal immigrant from Venezuela.
Fox told lawmakers her daughter was thrown headfirst into a concrete barrier at nearly 50 mph and that the driver and passenger fled without checking whether she was alive.
"Despite her initial prognosis, Carissa survived. Praise God, but survival and recovery are not the same," Fox testified.

Patricia Fox speaks during an event at U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement headquarters on April 9, 2026, in Washington, D.C. Fox's daughter, 22-year-old Carissa Aspnes, was left permanently disabled after an undocumented immigrant crashed into her with a car. (Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images)

Fox said she now uses a Hoyer lift to get her adult daughter out of bed because Aspnes cannot sit up or stand on her own. She said she blends her daughter’s food and feeds her through a G-tube, administers her medications and bathes her, while sleeping lightly at night in case her pulse oximeter sounds an alarm.
"One collision created an entire family of victims," Fox said, arguing that her daughter’s case carried an additional source of anguish because of the accused driver’s immigration status.
"If an American citizen had hit my daughter, I wouldn't be here asking, ‘Why was somebody who had no lawful right to be in this country here to hit her in the first place?’" Fox said.
Fox later delivered a pointed message about the partisan divide over immigration policy, telling lawmakers that cases like her daughter’s "shouldn’t be partisan."

"The lives of American citizens should matter to both sides," Fox said. "We get it. You guys hate Trump. The campaign ads, they're all the same. Taking the fight to Trump, standing against Trump, Trump, Trump, Trump.

Coleman also pointed to his wife, an immigrant who he said followed the legal process to come to the United States, while arguing that people who enter the country illegally should not be afforded the same treatment.
"My wife, an immigrant. She did what she's supposed to do," Coleman said. "She did exactly what she's supposed to do to get here."
Coleman saved one of his sharpest attacks for lawmakers who support sanctuary policies, telling them the consequences were sitting directly in front of them.

"I think that building needs to get checked for mold or something, because you guys are really out of your guys' mind thinking that sanctuary cities are the way to go," Coleman told the Democratic lawmakers.

title: Democrats blink in shutdown fight, hand Trump and GOP win before midterms
summary: House Democrats caved on their government shutdown push, but conservatives raged over a hemp ban delay and federal grants provision in the CR.
story: Fox News chief congressional correspondent Chad Pergram reports on the House of Representatives passing an avalanche of measures, including a budget bill to keep the government open until December 4th.
House Democrats relented to Republicans in their quest to prevent a government shutdown after spending months raising the possibility ahead of the crucial midterm elections.

Tuesday’s successful vote in the House, the second such attempt since July, means that lawmakers have officially punted funding the government until after the November election and are sending the short-term funding patch, known as a continuing resolution (CR), to President Donald Trump’s desk.

It also marks the end of months of concerns that House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., and Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., would again shut the government down for political gain as they vie for control of Congress.
DEMOCRATS BLINK AS SCHUMER HELPS GOP CLEAR KEY SHUTDOWN HURDLE

President Donald Trump gives a thumbs up before boarding Air Force One en route back to Washington, D.C., at Cleveland Hopkins International Airport in Cleveland on Aug. 11, 2026. (Jim Watson/AFP via Getty Images)
Both top Democrats caved on pushing for another shutdown, for now. And that gave House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., who needed Democratic votes to pass the bill, a win.
But while House Democrats agreed to support the bipartisan CR that passed the Senate last month, conservatives raged about certain changes that negotiators in the upper chamber wove into the bill.
Conservatives were outraged over an unrelated measure to delay a congressionally approved hemp product ban by 30 days and a provision curbing the Trump administration’s control over federal grants.
TRUMP COULD FACE IMPEACHMENT IF DEMOCRATS SEIZE HOUSE MAJORITY, GOP LEADER WARNS

House Freedom Caucus Chairman Andy Harris, R-Md., and members of Johnson’s right flank have criticized the CR over the hemp ban delay and grant rule change, a sentiment shared by Republicans in the Senate.

"The Senate did violence to our bill," Rep. Keith Self, R-Texas, told Fox News Digital. "Hemp and the grants are the two big ones…and frankly, I just don’t think CRs ought to be on suspension…when you put it on suspension, you’re not asking for my vote, okay, you’re going to get Democrats."
Voting on a bill under "suspension" means it gets fast-tracked past multiple procedural hurdles in exchange for raising the threshold for passage from a simple majority to two-thirds.
But the modification to the grant rule doesn’t permanently kill it.
SCHUMER CAVES, HANDS REPUBLICANS SHUTDOWN WIN AFTER MONTHS OF UNCERTAINTY
Rep. Andy Harris, chair of the Freedom Caucus, speaks to reporters alongside other members in the U.S. Capitol on March 27, 2026. (Samuel Corum/Getty Images)

Senate Republicans were assured by the administration that the push for more control over federal grants could be ready to go by the time the stopgap expires in December. Democrats argue it could be used as a tool to dictate which states do and don't get federal dollars.
Meanwhile, the CR punts the deadline to avert a government shutdown to Dec. 11, giving lawmakers a little over a month to create a new federal budget for fiscal year 2027, which begins Oct. 1.

But House Appropriations Committee Chairman Tom Cole, R-Okla., whose panel is in charge of writing those spending bills along with its Senate counterpart, told Fox News Digital that would not be enough time.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
He placed blame squarely on Senate Democrats, who he argued were trying to hinder Senate Appropriations Committee Chairwoman Susan Collins, R-Maine, and her bid for re-election come November.

"They clearly do not want Susan Collins to have any success. So all of America has to suffer until they figure out who's going to win in Maine," Cole said. "We're going to risk a year-long CR, if not a shutdown. So they've just been incredibly irresponsible."
Alex Miller is a writer for Fox News Digital covering the U.S. Senate.

title: NY Gov Kathy Hochul accuses Trump of 'defunding the police,' says DHS is 'withholding' counterterror funds
summary: New York Gov. Kathy Hochul accused President Donald Trump of "defunding the police," saying that DHS is "withholding" millions of dollars in funding.
story: New York Gov. Kathy Hochul accused President Donald Trump of "defunding the police" while accusing the Department of Homeland Security of "withholding" counterterrorism funding.

Ahead of the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 terrorist attacks, New York Gov. Kathy Hochul accused President Donald Trump's Department of Homeland Security of "withholding" millions of dollars in counterterrorism funding.

"The Department of Homeland Security, the agency created in response to 9/11, is withholding 40% of New York State's counterterrorism funding," Hochul asserted during a press conference with New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani on Tuesday.

"Because if you don't release the counterterrorism funding, you're betraying every family that lost someone on 9/11. You're betraying every police officer and firefighter who puts their lives on the line every single day. And you're betraying every New Yorker who no longer believes that the federal government is there to protect them," she said.

Mamdani declared that "the federal government's refusal to provide $87 million in critical public safety and emergency readiness funding that was promised is so unacceptable."
RETIRED PORT AUTHORITY OFFICERS TELL MAMDANI, HOCHUL TO STAY AWAY FROM GROUND ZERO ON 9/11
Mayor Zohran Mamdani speaks during a press conference following a fatal stabbing in Times Square in Manhattan, New York, on Aug. 31, 2026. (Kyle Mazza/Anadolu via Getty Images)

"We are talking about the money needed to fully fund 12 bomb squads across New York. We are talking about the money needed to ensure that in the event of a catastrophic attack, the FDNY can communicate internally and respond effectively. title: El-Sayed torched online after uneasy union member struggles through campaign event
summary: A UAW worker's struggle at Abdul El-Sayed's Michigan Senate press conference sparked a fierce debate between conservative and liberal commentators on X.
story: A woman speaking at a campaign event for Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed went viral after appearing nervous while on stage. (Credit: WJBK)

A woman delivering remarks at a news conference held by Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed on Monday appeared visibly nervous and repeatedly paused during her speech, prompting a wave of speculation on social media about the reason for her unease.

The woman, whom El-Sayed's staff identified as a union member employed by a truck factory, paused at multiple points during her speech, was breathing heavily and appeared uneasy. El-Sayed and Democratic State Sen. Mallory McMorrow both attempted to comfort the woman as she trudged through her remarks.

Some conservative commentators on social media questioned whether the woman had been coerced into speaking at the event, while others used the moment to criticize El-Sayed's campaign organization. These claims drew the ire of Mallory McMorrow, who ran against El-Sayed in the state’s Democratic primary but has since endorsed his candidacy.

"She had never spoken at a press conference before. Beforehand, she shared with me that she was really nervous. But she told me it was important for her to be there as a UAW member because she believed in using her voice for her fellow members and for working families," the state senator wrote on X. "But the way you all are tearing her apart … It's callous, cruel and it's no wonder why so many people absolutely despise this moment that we're in."
DEMOCRATS' CIVIL WAR HEADS TO MICHIGAN WHERE PROGRESSIVES FACE BIGGEST TEST YET IN HIGH-STAKES SENATE SHOWDOWN

US Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed speaks during a press conference in Detroit, Mich., on Aug. 5, 2026, after narrowly winning the Michigan Democratic Senate nomination. He was flanked by Michigan State Sen. Mallory McMorrow and Michigan Democratic Party Chair Curtis Hertel Jr. (AFP via Getty Images)
Some commentators focused on the union member's race, tying the episode to broader criticism of El-Sayed's support among Black voters in the Democratic primary.
BLACK VOTERS RIP DEMS OVER TAKING THEM FOR GRANTED IN EL-SAYED'S BACKYARD: ‘HUSH US UP’
Mallory McMorrow campaigns at the Michigan Democratic Nominating Convention in Detroit on April 19, 2026. (Jim West/UCG/Universal Images Group)
"Abdul's support from black Michiganders summed up perfectly in 40 seconds," radio host and conservative columnist Derek Hunter wrote on X.
"The El Sayed campaign is in free fall," Trump administration official Richard Grenell said.
Others questioned whether the woman even wanted to be speaking at a campaign event.
"Are they holding a gun to her back?" an organization purporting to represent Democrats backing GOP Senate nominee Mike Rogers posted in response to the clip.
"She seems to be under duress! Looks like she’s being coerced into speaking. Very eerie!" conservative commentator Link Lauren wrote.
"Is it just me or does she look hostage-level nervous?" another X user asked.

MICHIGAN DEMOCRAT MALLORY MCMORROW DROPS OUT OF SENATE RACE WEEKS BEFORE PRIMARY
Abdul El-Sayed, a Democratic Senate candidate in Michigan, speaks to supporters at a campaign event, on August 2, 2026, in Detroit, Michigan (Paul Steinhauser/Fox News)

title: FBI agents confront Swalwell at airport in new footage as viewers zero in and pile on

story: Video shows FBI agents swarming former Rep. Eric Swalwell during a criminal investaigtion and seizing his electronic devices at San Francisco Airport. (Credit: Obtained by CA Post, Aug. 15)
New footage shows former Rep. Eric Swalwell being met by FBI agents at San Francisco International Airport, prompting criticism and mockery on social media.
The video, first obtained by the California Post, shows Swalwell sporting a black sweatshirt and hat deboarding a plane where FBI agents met him at his gate on Aug. 15.

The FBI seized Swalwell’s cellphone and laptop at the airport on Aug. 15, according to Fox News Digital’s previous reporting. Swalwell resigned from Congress in April amid allegations of sexual misconduct.
The FBI searched his Washington, D.C., home the following day, Fox News Digital previously reported.

title: Uber lets parents watch teen rides live
summary: Uber teen accounts now feature live video streaming from the driver's camera, but encrypted recordings stay on Uber's servers for up to 14 days.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
School, soccer practice, a shift at work or a friend's house. Teens have places to go, and parents can't always be there for every ride. Uber is giving families a new way to check in.

The company is adding live video streaming to Uber Teen Accounts, allowing a linked parent or guardian to see their teen inside the vehicle during an active ride. The feed comes from the front-facing camera on the driver's smartphone.
Uber says the feature is live now in nine U.S. markets. Uber plans a nationwide rollout over the coming weeks.

If you have a teen who uses Uber, the idea may sound reassuring. However, a live camera inside the car also raises privacy questions. Who can watch? Does Uber see the stream? What happens to the video after the ride? Uber gave CyberGuy more detail on exactly how the feature works.

HOUSTON UBER DRIVER CAUGHT IN WILD POLICE CHASE AS OFFICERS SEEN ON DASHCAM VIDEO HITCHING A RIDE IN HIS CAR
Uber is adding live video to Teen Accounts, allowing linked parents or guardians to check on teens during active rides. (Klaudia Radecka/NurPhoto via Getty Images)
How Uber Teen Accounts live video works

Uber launched Teen Accounts in 2023 to give teenagers more independence while keeping their rides connected to a parent or guardian. Now, live video adds another option for families who want more visibility during a trip.

If a driver has live video enabled, Uber sends a push notification to the parent or guardian linked to the teen's account when the ride begins. The parent can tap the notification and watch the live feed through the driver's front-facing smartphone camera.

Uber says both the teen and the driver receive a notification when the parent begins watching. Everyone inside the vehicle knows when the livestream is active. Only the parent or guardian linked to the teen's account can view the live video during the trip, according to Uber. Uber also told CyberGuy that the company cannot access the live video in real time.
Where Uber teen live video is available
The feature is starting in a limited number of U.S. markets before expanding more broadly.
Uber told CyberGuy that live video is currently available in:
AtlantaPhoenixOrlandoRaleigh-DurhamPortland, OregonSan AntonioClevelandRhode IslandEl Paso
Atlanta
